lessons.title: Review Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The zero matrix [[0, 0], [0, 0]] is the identity matrix with respect to addition.
  • A diagonal matrix has all non-diagonal entries zero; a scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix with all diagonal entries equal.
  • Formulas |A| = ad - bc, adj A = [[d, -b], [-c, a]] and A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj A are used throughout the review.
  • A matrix is not invertible exactly when its determinant is 0.
  • Adding matrices of order 2 x 5 gives a matrix of order 2 x 5.
  • Systems in the review are solved by X = A^-1 B and checked by substitution.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Choose the correct answer. [0 0]
[0 0] is

Options: (a) an identity matrix w.r.t multiplication (b) a column matrix (c) an identity matrix w.r.t addition (d) a row matrix

Correct answer: an identity matrix w.r.t addition

Q: Q1(ii). Choose the correct answer. [4 0]
[0 -12] is

Options: (a) a scalar matrix (b) 2 × 3 matrix (c) a diagonal matrix (d) None of these

Correct answer: a diagonal matrix

Q: Q1(iii). Choose the correct answer. If A = [-1 -2]
[3 1], then adj A =

Options: (a) [-1 -2] [3 1] (b) [1 2] [-3 -1] (c) [-1 2] [3 1] (d) [1 -2] [3 1]

Correct answer: [1 2] [-3 -1]

Q: Q1(iv). Choose the correct answer. If A = [2 3]
[3 4], then A^-1 =

Options: (a) [4 3] [-3 2] (b) [4 -3] [-3 2] (c) [-2 3] [3 -4] (d) [-4 3] [3 -2]

Correct answer: [-4 3] [3 -2]

Q: Q1(v). Choose the correct answer. [5 1.5]
[2 d] is not invertible, when d =

Options: (a) -0.6 (b) 0 (c) 0.6 (d) 3

Correct answer: 0.6

Q: Q1(vi). Choose the correct answer. If A and B are matrices of order 2 × 5, then the dimensions of A + B are

Options: (a) 2 × 5 (b) 10 × 10 (c) 7 × 1 (d) 7 × 7

Correct answer: 2 × 5

Q: Q1(vii). Choose the correct answer. The multiplicative inverse of [1 2]
[0 1] is

Options: (a) [1 2] [0 1] (b) [1 -2] [0 1] (c) [-1 2] [0 1] (d) [1 -2] [0 -1]

Correct answer: [1 -2] [0 1]

Q: Q1(viii). Choose the correct answer. The determinant of the matrix [4 -1]
[-9 2] is

Options: (a) 17 (b) 1 (c) -1 (d) -17

Correct answer: -1

Q: Note

Ans: The book's printed Answers for Q1 above are wrong for six items. The printed key gives (ii) (a), (iii) (a), (iv) (c), (v) (b), (vii) (d) and (viii) (d). The correct options, marked in green above, are (ii) (c), (iii) (b), (iv) (d), (v) (c), (vii) (b) and (viii) (c). Each was verified by direct computation.

Q: Q2. Find x and y if [x-1 4]
[y+3 -7] = [0 4]
[-2 -7].

Ans: Rule: For equal matrices, the elements in corresponding positions must be equal.
From the (1,1) elements: x - 1 = 0, so x = 1.
From the (2,1) elements: y + 3 = -2, so y = -5.
The (1,2) and (2,2) elements are already equal (4 = 4 and -7 = -7).
Answer: x = 1, y = -5.

Q: Q3. Find the product of [1]
[-5]
[3] and [-6 5 8]
[0 4 -1] if possible.

Ans: Rule: A product XY is possible only if the number of columns of X equals the number of rows of Y.
The first matrix is 3 × 1, so it has 1 column.
The second matrix is 2 × 3, so it has 2 rows.
Columns of the first matrix (1) ≠ rows of the second matrix (2).
Answer: The product is not possible.

Q: Q4. Find the inverse of A = [6 -3]
[5 -2] if it exists.

Ans: Formula: A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj A, and the inverse exists only if |A| ≠ 0. For [a b]
[c d], |A| = ad - bc and adj A = [d -b]
[-c a].
|A| = 6 × (-2) - (-3) × 5 = -12 + 15 = 3 ≠ 0, so A^-1 exists.
adj A = [-2 3]
[-5 6].
A^-1 = (1/3)[-2 3]
[-5 6].
Answer: A^-1 = (1/3)[-2 3]
[-5 6].
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is A^-1 = (1/3)[-2 3]
[-5 6] (the printed key gives the unrelated matrix [11 13]
[3 5]).

Q: Q5. Solve the system of linear equations 2x + 5y = 9, 5x - 2y = 8.

Ans: Method (matrix inversion): Write the system as AX = B and find X = A^-1 B, where A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj A with |A| = ad - bc and adj A = [d -b]
[-c a].
In matrix form: [2 5]
[5 -2] × [x]
[y] = [9]
[8], so A = [2 5]
[5 -2], B = [9]
[8].
|A| = 2 × (-2) - 5 × 5 = -4 - 25 = -29 ≠ 0, so A^-1 exists.
adj A = [-2 -5]
[-5 2], so A^-1 = (1/-29)[-2 -5]
[-5 2] = (1/29)[2 5]
[5 -2].
X = A^-1 B = (1/29)[2 5]
[5 -2] × [9]
[8] = (1/29)[2×9+5×8]
[5×9-2×8] = (1/29)[58]
[29] = [2]
[1].
Check: 2(2) + 5(1) = 9 ✓ and 5(2) - 2(1) = 8 ✓.
Answer: x = 2, y = 1.
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is x = 2, y = 1 (the printed key gives (-2, 5), which does not satisfy the equations).

Q: Q6. A man paid Rs 203 for 3 small boxes and 14 large boxes. If he had bought 11 small boxes and 11 large boxes, he would have paid Rs 220. Find the cost of a small box and a large box.

Ans: Method: Let the cost of one small box be Rs x and the cost of one large box be Rs y, form two linear equations, write them as AX = B and solve by X = A^-1 B, where A^-1 = (1/|A|) adj A.
First purchase: 3x + 14y = 203.
Second purchase: 11x + 11y = 220.
In matrix form: [3 14]
[11 11] × [x]
[y] = [203]
[220], so A = [3 14]
[11 11], B = [203]
[220].
|A| = 3 × 11 - 14 × 11 = 33 - 154 = -121 ≠ 0, so A^-1 exists.
adj A = [11 -14]
[-11 3], so A^-1 = (1/-121)[11 -14]
[-11 3] = (1/121)[-11 14]
[11 -3].
X = A^-1 B = (1/121)[-11 14]
[11 -3] × [203]
[220] = (1/121)[-11×203+14×220]
[11×203-3×220] = (1/121)[-2233+3080]
[2233-660] = (1/121)[847]
[1573] = [7]
[13].
Check: 3(7) + 14(13) = 21 + 182 = 203 ✓ and 11(7) + 11(13) = 77 + 143 = 220 ✓.
Answer: A small box costs Rs 7 and a large box costs Rs 13.

mcqs.q: The matrix [[0, 0], [0, 0]] is:
mcqs.why: Adding the zero matrix to any matrix leaves it unchanged: A + O = A. So O is the additive identity. The multiplicative identity is [[1, 0], [0, 1]], not the zero matrix.

mcqs.q: The matrix [[4, 0], [0, -12]] is:
mcqs.why: All entries off the main diagonal are 0, so it is diagonal. It is not scalar because the diagonal entries 4 and -12 are not equal. The book key wrongly keys this as a scalar matrix.

mcqs.q: If A = [[-1, -2], [3, 1]], then adj A is:
mcqs.why: adj A = [[d, -b], [-c, a]] with a = -1, b = -2, c = 3, d = 1: [[1, -(-2)], [-3, -1]] = [[1, 2], [-3, -1]]. The book key wrongly gives A itself.

mcqs.q: The matrix [[5, 1.5], [2, d]] is not invertible when d equals:
mcqs.why: Not invertible means determinant 0: |A| = 5d - 1.5x2 = 5d - 3 = 0, so d = 3/5 = 0.6. The book key wrongly gives d = 0.

mcqs.q: If A and B are matrices of order 2 x 5, then the dimensions of A + B are:
mcqs.why: Matrices of the same order are added element by element, and the sum keeps that order. Both are 2 x 5, so A + B is 2 x 5.

mcqs.q: The multiplicative inverse of [[1, 2], [0, 1]] is:
The determinant of [[4, -1], [-9, 2]] is:
mcqs.why: Formula ad - bc: 4x2 - (-1)(-9) = 8 - 9 = -1. Careful: (-1)(-9) = +9, and it is subtracted. The book key wrongly gives -17.
Equate corresponding elements: (1,1): x - 1 = 0 gives x = 1. (2,1): y + 3 = -2 gives y = -5. The other entries already match (4 = 4, -7 = -7).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Natural numbers are the counting numbers 1, 2, 3, ...; whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3, ...
  • Integers are ..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ... (whole numbers together with their negatives).
  • A rational number can be written as p/q with p, q integers and q not 0; every integer, terminating decimal and recurring decimal is rational.
  • An irrational number cannot be written as p/q; its decimal is non-terminating and non-repeating, e.g. sqrt(3), sqrt(7), pi.
  • Real numbers R = Q union Q': every rational or irrational number is real. Note sqrt(36) = 6, so it is natural, whole, integer and rational.
  • A fraction gives a terminating decimal if the division ends with remainder 0, otherwise a non-terminating recurring decimal, e.g. 1/8 = 0.125 but 1/6 = 0.1666...

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are whole numbers?

Ans: Rule: Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3, ... (non-negative integers).
First simplify: √36 = 6, which is a whole number.
Check each given number one by one.
2 is a whole number.
5 is a whole number.
3 is a whole number.
5/7, -1.96 and -7/6 are not integers, so they are not whole numbers.
√36 = 6 is a whole number.
√3, √7, -√14 and π are irrational, so they are not whole numbers.
-9 is negative, so it is not a whole number.
1 is a whole number.
4 2/3 and 0.333... are not integers.
Answer: 2, 5, 3, √36, 1
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 2, 5, 3, √36, 1. The printed key (3, 0, √36, 1) omits 2 and 5 and includes 0, which is not among the given numbers.

Q: Q2. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are integers?

Ans: Rule: Integers are ..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ... (whole numbers and their negatives).
First simplify: √36 = 6, which is an integer.
2, 5 and 3 are integers.
√36 = 6 is an integer.
-9 is an integer.
1 is an integer.
5/7, -1.96, -7/6, 4 2/3 and 0.333... are fractions/decimals, not integers.
√3, √7, -√14 and π are irrational, not integers.
Answer: 2, 5, 3, √36, -9, 1
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 2, 5, 3, √36, -9, 1. The printed key (3, 0, √36, -9, 1) omits 2 and 5 and includes 0, which is not among the given numbers.

Q: Q3. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are irrational numbers?

Ans: Rule: An irrational number cannot be written in the form p/q; its decimal never terminates and never repeats.
√3 = 1.732050... is non-terminating and non-repeating, so it is irrational.
√7 = 2.645751... is irrational.
-√14 = -3.741657... is irrational.
π = 3.141592... is irrational.
All the other given numbers are integers, fractions or terminating/recurring decimals, so they are rational.
Note √36 = 6, an integer, so √36 is rational, not irrational.
Answer: √3, √7, -√14, π

Q: Q4. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are natural numbers?

Ans: Rule: Natural numbers are the counting numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, ...
First simplify: √36 = 6, a natural number.
2, 5 and 3 are natural numbers.
1 is a natural number.
-9 is negative, so it is not natural.
5/7, -1.96, -7/6, 4 2/3 and 0.333... are not counting numbers.
√3, √7, -√14 and π are irrational, so they are not natural.
Answer: 2, 5, 3, √36, 1
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 2, 5, 3, √36, 1. The printed key (3, √36, 1) omits the natural numbers 2 and 5.

Q: Q5. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are rational numbers?

Ans: Rule: A rational number can be written in the form p/q, where p, q are integers and q ≠ 0. Every integer, terminating decimal and recurring decimal is rational.
2 = 2/1, 5 = 5/1, 3 = 3/1 and 1 = 1/1 are rational.
5/7 and -7/6 are already in p/q form, so they are rational.
-1.96 = -196/100 is rational.
√36 = 6 = 6/1 is rational.
-9 = -9/1 is rational.
4 2/3 = 14/3 is rational.
0.333... is a recurring decimal, so it is rational (= 1/3).
√3, √7, -√14 and π cannot be written as p/q, so they are not rational.
Answer: 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, -9, 1, 4 2/3, 0.333...
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, -9, 1, 4 2/3, 0.333... The printed key includes 0 and 2.5, neither of which is among the given numbers.

Q: Q6. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are real numbers?

Ans: Rule: The set of real numbers R is the union of the rational and irrational numbers, R = Q ∪ Q'.
Every given number is either rational or irrational.
Hence every given number lies on the number line and is real.
Answer: All of them — 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333...

Q: Q7. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are rational numbers but not integers?

Ans: Rule: First pick the rational numbers, then remove the integers from them.
The rational numbers in the list are 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, -9, 1, 4 2/3, 0.333...
The integers among them are 2, 5, 3, √36 (= 6), -9 and 1.
Removing these leaves the fractions and decimals.
Answer: 5/7, -1.96, -7/6, 4 2/3, 0.333...
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 5/7, -1.96, -7/6, 4 2/3, 0.333... The printed key also includes 2.5, which is not among the given numbers.

Q: Q8. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are integers but not whole numbers?

Ans: Rule: Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3, ...; so an integer that is not whole must be a negative integer.
The integers in the list are 2, 5, 3, √36 (= 6), -9 and 1.
Of these, only -9 is negative.
Answer: -9

Q: Q9. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are integers but not natural numbers?

Ans: Rule: Natural numbers are 1, 2, 3, ...; so an integer that is not natural is 0 or a negative integer.
The integers in the list are 2, 5, 3, √36 (= 6), -9 and 1.
0 is not among the given numbers.
The only one that is not natural is -9.
Answer: -9
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is -9. The printed key (0, -9) includes 0, which is not among the given numbers.

Q: Q10. From the numbers 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, √36, -7/6, √3, -9, 1, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... — Which are real numbers but not integers?

Ans: Rule: First take all the real numbers (the whole list), then remove the integers.
The integers in the list are 2, 5, 3, √36 (= 6), -9 and 1.
Removing these leaves all the fractions, decimals and irrational numbers.
Answer: 5/7, -1.96, -7/6, √3, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333...
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 5/7, -1.96, -7/6, √3, √7, -√14, π, 4 2/3, 0.333... The printed key also includes 2.5, which is not among the given numbers.

Q: Q11(i). Write the decimal representation of 1/6.

Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator; a remainder that repeats gives a recurring decimal.
1 ÷ 6 = 0.1, remainder 4.
40 ÷ 6 = 6, remainder 4.
The remainder 4 repeats, so the digit 6 repeats forever.
1/6 = 0.1666...
Answer: 0.1666... (non-terminating recurring decimal)

Q: Q11(ii). Write the decimal representation of 5/6.

Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator; a remainder that repeats gives a recurring decimal.
5 ÷ 6 = 0.8, remainder 2.
20 ÷ 6 = 3, remainder 2.
The remainder 2 repeats, so the digit 3 repeats forever.
5/6 = 0.8333...
Answer: 0.8333... (non-terminating recurring decimal)

Q: Q11(iii). Write the decimal representation of 2/9.

Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator; a remainder that repeats gives a recurring decimal.
2 ÷ 9 = 0.2, remainder 2.
The remainder 2 is the same as the start, so the digit 2 repeats forever.
2/9 = 0.222...
Answer: 0.222... (non-terminating recurring decimal)

Q: Q11(iv). Write the decimal representation of 1/8.

Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator; if the remainder becomes zero, the decimal terminates.
1 ÷ 8 = 0.1, remainder 2.
20 ÷ 8 = 2, remainder 4.
40 ÷ 8 = 5, remainder 0.
The remainder is zero, so the division ends.
1/8 = 0.125
Answer: 0.125 (terminating decimal)

Q: Q12(i). Depict 1/3 on a number line.

Ans: Rule: To depict a fraction on the number line, first write it as a decimal and mark its position between the two nearest integers.
1/3 = 0.333...
0.333... lies between 0 and 1.
It is one third of the way from 0 towards 1.
Mark the point at distance 1/3 from 0 on the right side of 0.
Answer: The point for 1/3 (≈ 0.33) lies between 0 and 1, at one-third of the unit length from 0.

Q: Q12(ii). Depict 1/4 on a number line.

Ans: Rule: To depict a fraction on the number line, first write it as a decimal and mark its position between the two nearest integers.
1/4 = 0.25
0.25 lies between 0 and 1.
It is one quarter of the way from 0 towards 1.
Mark the point at distance 1/4 from 0 on the right side of 0.
Answer: The point for 1/4 (0.25) lies between 0 and 1, at one-quarter of the unit length from 0.

Q: Q12(iii). Depict 1/9 on a number line.

Ans: Rule: To depict a fraction on the number line, first write it as a decimal and mark its position between the two nearest integers.
1/9 = 0.111...
0.111... lies between 0 and 1, very close to 0.
It lies just to the right of 1/10 and well to the left of 1/4.
Mark the point at distance 1/9 from 0 on the right side of 0.
Answer: The point for 1/9 (≈ 0.11) lies between 0 and 1, at one-ninth of the unit length from 0.

Q: Q12(iv). Depict 1/10 on a number line.

Ans: Rule: To depict a fraction on the number line, first write it as a decimal and mark its position between the two nearest integers.
1/10 = 0.1
0.1 lies between 0 and 1, close to 0.
Divide the unit length from 0 to 1 into 10 equal parts and take the first mark.
Answer: The point for 1/10 (0.1) lies between 0 and 1, at one-tenth of the unit length from 0. In increasing order the four points of Q12 are 1/10, 1/9, 1/4, 1/3.

mcqs.q: From the list 2, 5, 3, 5/7, -1.96, sqrt(36), -7/6, sqrt(3), -9, 1, sqrt(7), -sqrt(14), pi, 4 2/3, 0.333..., the whole numbers are:
mcqs.why: Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3, ... First sqrt(36) = 6, a whole number. From the list: 2, 5, 3, 6 (as sqrt(36)) and 1 qualify. -9 is negative and the fractions/decimals/irrationals are not integers. The book key wrongly omits 2 and 5 and includes 0, which is not in the list.

mcqs.q: From the same list, the irrational numbers are:
mcqs.why: Irrationals have non-terminating, non-repeating decimals: sqrt(3) = 1.732050..., sqrt(7) = 2.645751..., -sqrt(14) = -3.741657..., pi = 3.141592... . Note sqrt(36) = 6 is rational, not irrational.

mcqs.q: From the same list, the integers are:
mcqs.why: Integers include negatives: 2, 5, 3 are integers; sqrt(36) = 6 is an integer; -9 is an integer; 1 is an integer. Fractions, decimals like -1.96 and 0.333..., and irrationals are not integers. The book key wrongly omits 2 and 5.

mcqs.q: From the same list, the rational numbers but not integers are:
mcqs.why: Take the rationals, then remove the integers 2, 5, 3, 6, -9, 1. What remains: 5/7 and -7/6 (already p/q), -1.96 = -196/100, 4 2/3 = 14/3, and the recurring decimal 0.333... = 1/3. The book key wrongly adds 2.5, which is not in the list.

mcqs.q: From the same list, the integer that is not a whole number is:
mcqs.why: Integers in the list are 2, 5, 3, 6, -9, 1. Whole numbers are non-negative, so the only integer that fails to be whole is the negative integer -9.

mcqs.q: The decimal representation of 1/6 is:
mcqs.why: Divide: 1 / 6 = 0.1 remainder 4; 40 / 6 = 6 remainder 4. The remainder 4 repeats, so the digit 6 repeats forever: 1/6 = 0.1666..., a non-terminating recurring decimal, hence rational.

mcqs.q: The decimal representation of 1/8 is:
mcqs.why: Divide: 1 / 8 = 0.1 rem 2; 20 / 8 = 2 rem 4; 40 / 8 = 5 rem 0. The remainder becomes 0, so the decimal terminates: 1/8 = 0.125.

mcqs.q: The decimal representation of 5/6 is:
mcqs.why: Divide: 5 / 6 = 0.8 remainder 2; 20 / 6 = 3 remainder 2. The remainder 2 repeats, so 3 repeats: 5/6 = 0.8333..., a non-terminating recurring decimal.

mcqs.q: On the number line, the points 1/10, 1/9, 1/4, 1/3 in increasing order are:
Every number in the list (including sqrt(3) and pi) is a real number because:
options: Real numbers are exactly the rationals together with the irrationals
mcqs.why: By definition R = Q union Q': the reals consist of all rationals plus all irrationals. Each listed number is one or the other, so all of them are real and lie on the number line.

lessons.title: Activity (p.60)
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Division does NOT distribute over addition in the denominator: a/(b + c) is not equal to a/b + a/c.
  • The distributive law belongs to multiplication over addition, not to splitting a denominator.
  • In Mahnoor's working, Line 1 (40/9 = 40/(4+5)) is correct but Line 2 (= 40/4 + 40/5) is wrong, so Lines 3 and 4 that follow from it are also wrong.
  • The correct value is 40/9 = 4.444... which is approximately 4.44, as Tahira said.
  • Check: 40/4 + 40/5 = 10 + 8 = 18, which is far from 40/9, confirming the split is invalid.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Mahnoor wanted to work out 40/9 without a calculator. She wrote: Line 1: 40/9 = 40/(4 + 5); Line 2: = 40/4 + 40/5; Line 3: = 10 + 8; Line 4: = 18. Her friend Tahira said the correct answer should be 4.44. Which line of Mahnoor's working was wrong? Who was correct?

Ans: Rule: Division does not distribute over addition in the denominator: a/(b + c) ≠ a/b + a/c. The distributive law applies to multiplication over addition, not to splitting a denominator.
Line 1 is correct: 9 = 4 + 5, so 40/9 = 40/(4 + 5).
Line 2 is wrong: 40/(4 + 5) cannot be split into 40/4 + 40/5.
Because of this, Lines 3 and 4, which follow from Line 2, are also wrong.
Correct working: 40/9 = 4.444... ≈ 4.44.
Answer: Line 2 was wrong; Tahira was correct, 40/9 ≈ 4.44.

mcqs.q: Mahnoor wrote 40/9 = 40/(4+5) = 40/4 + 40/5 = 10 + 8 = 18. Which line was wrong?
options: No line was wrong; 18 is correct
mcqs.why: Line 1 is correct since 9 = 4 + 5. Line 2 splits the denominator, claiming 40/(4+5) = 40/4 + 40/5, which is false. Lines 3 and 4 follow correctly from Line 2, so the single wrong step is Line 2.

mcqs.q: The correct value of 40/9 is:
mcqs.why: Divide: 40 / 9 = 4 remainder 4, and the remainder repeats, giving 4.444... . Rounded to two decimal places this is 4.44, as Tahira said. It is nowhere near 18.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true in general?
options: a/(b + c) = a/b + a/c for all a, b, c
Division distributes over addition in the denominator
a/(b + c) is not equal to a/b + a/c in general
mcqs.why: Counterexample from the activity: a = 40, b = 4, c = 5 gives a/(b+c) = 40/9 = 4.444... but a/b + a/c = 10 + 8 = 18. Since 4.444... differs from 18, division does not distribute over a denominator sum.
Compute each term: 40/4 = 10 and 40/5 = 8. Add: 10 + 8 = 18. This is the value Mahnoor obtained, and it differs from 40/9, proving her split was invalid.

mcqs.q: Who was correct about 40/9?
mcqs.why: Direct division gives 40/9 = 4.444... = 4.44 to two decimal places, exactly Tahira's value. Mahnoor's 18 came from the invalid denominator split in Line 2.

mcqs.q: Line 1 of the working, 40/9 = 40/(4 + 5), is:
options: Wrong, because division cannot be written with brackets
Correct only if the answer is 18
mcqs.why: 4 + 5 = 9, so replacing 9 by (4 + 5) does not change the value: 40/9 = 40/(4+5). The error comes later, when the denominator is split in Line 2.

mcqs.q: Which of the following correctly applies a distributive idea?
mcqs.why: Multiplication distributes over addition: (4+5) x 40 = 9 x 40 = 360 and 4x40 + 5x40 = 160 + 200 = 360, equal. The other three split a denominator, which is exactly the invalid step from the activity.

mcqs.q: Using the same (wrong) splitting method, 20/(2 + 3) would give 20/2 + 20/3 = 16.67 approx, but the true value of 20/(2+3) is:
mcqs.why: True value: denominator 2 + 3 = 5, so 20/5 = 4. The split value 16.67 is completely different, confirming again that a denominator sum cannot be split into separate divisions.

mcqs.q: The distributive law a(b + c) = ab + ac applies to:
mcqs.why: The law states that a factor multiplied by a sum equals the sum of the separate products: a(b+c) = ab + ac. It is about multiplication. Division by (b + c) is multiplication by 1/(b+c) as a whole, not separate divisions by b and c.

mcqs.q: A quick check that 40/9 cannot be 18 is:
mcqs.why: If 40/9 were 18, then 18 x 9 would equal 40. But 18 x 9 = 162, not 40. Whereas 4.444... x 9 = 40 exactly, confirming 40/9 = 4.444... and exposing Line 2's error.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Associative property of addition: a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c; only the grouping changes.
  • Associative property of multiplication: a x (b x c) = (a x b) x c.
  • Distributive property: a(b + c) = ab + ac, e.g. 5(a + b) = 5a + 5b.
  • Additive identity: a + 0 = 0 + a = a; 0 is the additive identity.
  • Multiplicative inverse: a x (1/a) = 1; e.g. 5 x 1/5 = 1, so 5 and 1/5 are inverses of each other.
  • The distributive property gives quick calculations, e.g. 39 x 63 + 39 x 37 = 39 x 100 = 3900.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Name the property used in the equation: 1 + (4 + 3) = (1 + 4) + 3

Ans: Rule: Associative property w.r.t addition: a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c.
Only the grouping (brackets) has changed; the order of the numbers is the same.
This is exactly the associative pattern with a = 1, b = 4, c = 3.
Answer: Associative property w.r.t addition

Q: Q1(ii). Name the property used in the equation: 5(a + b) = 5a + 5b

Ans: Rule: Distributive property of multiplication over addition: a(b + c) = ab + ac.
The factor 5 outside the bracket is multiplied by each term inside the bracket.
5 × a = 5a and 5 × b = 5b.
Answer: Distributive property of multiplication over addition

Q: Q1(iii). Name the property used in the equation: a + 0 = 0 + a = a

Ans: Rule: Additive identity: a + 0 = 0 + a = a, where 0 is the additive identity.
Adding 0 to a leaves a unchanged.
Answer: Additive identity (0 is the additive identity)

Q: Q1(iv). Name the property used in the equation: 5 × 1/5 = 1/5 × 5 = 1

Ans: Rule: Multiplicative inverse: a × a⁻¹ = a⁻¹ × a = 1, where a⁻¹ = 1/a.
Here 5 × (1/5) = 1.
So 5 and 1/5 are multiplicative inverses of each other (the equality of the two orders also uses commutativity of multiplication).
Answer: Multiplicative inverse

Q: Q2(i). Write the missing number: 2 + (---- + 4) = (2 + 6) + 4

Ans: Rule: Associative property w.r.t addition: a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c.
Compare both sides: on the right side the first two numbers grouped are 2 and 6.
So on the left side the number grouped with 4 must be 6.
2 + (6 + 4) = (2 + 6) + 4
Answer: 6

Q: Q2(ii). Write the missing number: 7 + (4 + 2) = 13, so (7 + 4) + 2 = ----

Ans: Rule: Associative property w.r.t addition: changing the grouping does not change the sum.
7 + (4 + 2) = 7 + 6 = 13.
(7 + 4) + 2 has the same three numbers with different grouping.
So (7 + 4) + 2 = 13.
Answer: 13

Q: Q2(iii). Write the missing number: 9 × (3 × 4) = 108, so (9 × 3) × 4 = ----

Ans: Rule: Associative property w.r.t multiplication: changing the grouping does not change the product.
9 × (3 × 4) = 9 × 12 = 108.
(9 × 3) × 4 has the same three numbers with different grouping.
So (9 × 3) × 4 = 108.
Answer: 108

Q: Q2(iv). Write the missing number: 5 × (8 × 9) = (5 × ----) × 9

Ans: Rule: Associative property w.r.t multiplication: a × (b × c) = (a × b) × c.
Compare both sides: on the left side the numbers grouped are 8 and 9.
So on the right side 5 must be grouped with 8.
5 × (8 × 9) = (5 × 8) × 9
Answer: 8

Q: Q3(i). Choose the correct option: 8 × (6 × 7) is equal to:

Options: (a) 8 × 6 - 7 (b) 8 - (6 - 7) (c) 8 × 12 (d) (8 × 6) × 7

Correct answer: (8 × 6) × 7

Q: Q3(ii). Choose the correct option: Which one of the following illustrates the Associative Law of addition?

Options: (a) 3 + (2 + 4) = (4 + 4) + 1 (b) 3 + (2 + 4) = (3 + 2) + 4 (c) 3 + (2 + 4) = (5 + 2) + 2 (d) 3 + (2 + 4) = (2 + 6) + 1

Correct answer: 3 + (2 + 4) = (3 + 2) + 4

Q: Q3(iii). Choose the correct option: Which of the following illustrates the Associative Law of multiplication?

Options: (a) 4 × (3 × 6) = (6 × 6) × 2 (b) 4 × (3 × 6) = (3 × 12) × 2 (c) 4 × (3 × 6) = (4 × 3) × 6 (d) 4 × (3 × 6) = (3 × 8) × 3

Correct answer: 4 × (3 × 6) = (4 × 3) × 6

Q: Q4(i). Do this with and without using distributive property: 39 × 63 + 39 × 37

Ans: Rule: Distributive property: a × b + a × c = a × (b + c).
Without distributive property:
39 × 63 = 2457
39 × 37 = 1443
2457 + 1443 = 3900
With distributive property:
39 × 63 + 39 × 37 = 39 × (63 + 37)
= 39 × 100
= 3900
Both methods agree.
Answer: 3900

Q: Q4(ii). Do this with and without using distributive property: 81 × 450 + 81 × 550

Ans: Rule: Distributive property: a × b + a × c = a × (b + c).
Without distributive property:
81 × 450 = 36450
81 × 550 = 44550
36450 + 44550 = 81000
With distributive property:
81 × 450 + 81 × 550 = 81 × (450 + 550)
= 81 × 1000
= 81000
Both methods agree.
Answer: 81000

Q: Q4(iii). Do this with and without using distributive property: 50 × 161 - 50 × 81

Ans: Rule: Distributive property: a × b - a × c = a × (b - c).
Without distributive property:
50 × 161 = 8050
50 × 81 = 4050
8050 - 4050 = 4000
With distributive property:
50 × 161 - 50 × 81 = 50 × (161 - 81)
= 50 × 80
= 4000
Both methods agree.
Answer: 4000

Q: Q4(iv). Do this with and without using distributive property: 827 × 60 - 327 × 60

Ans: Rule: Distributive property: a × c - b × c = (a - b) × c.
Without distributive property:
827 × 60 = 49620
327 × 60 = 19620
49620 - 19620 = 30000
With distributive property:
827 × 60 - 327 × 60 = (827 - 327) × 60
= 500 × 60
= 30000
Both methods agree.
Answer: 30000

mcqs.q: The equation 1 + (4 + 3) = (1 + 4) + 3 uses:
mcqs.why: The numbers 1, 4, 3 keep the same order; only the brackets (grouping) move from (4+3) to (1+4). Regrouping in addition is the associative property: a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c.

mcqs.q: The equation 5(a + b) = 5a + 5b uses:
options: The distributive property of multiplication over addition
mcqs.why: The factor 5 outside the bracket is multiplied by each term inside: 5 x a = 5a and 5 x b = 5b. Spreading a multiplier over a sum is the distributive property.

mcqs.q: The equation a + 0 = 0 + a = a shows:
options: The additive identity; 0 is the additive identity
mcqs.why: Adding 0 leaves a unchanged: a + 0 = a. The number with this property for addition is 0, called the additive identity.

mcqs.q: In 2 + (---- + 4) = (2 + 6) + 4, the missing number is:
mcqs.why: By associativity a + (b + c) = (a + b) + c with a = 2, c = 4. On the right, 2 is grouped with 6, so on the left the number grouped with 4 must be b = 6.

mcqs.q: 8 x (6 x 7) is equal to:
mcqs.why: Associativity of multiplication regroups without changing the numbers or their order: 8 x (6 x 7) = (8 x 6) x 7. Both equal 8 x 42 = 336 and 48 x 7 = 336. (Book MCQ Q3(i), keyed correctly.)

mcqs.q: Which one illustrates the Associative Law of addition?
mcqs.why: Associativity keeps the same three numbers 3, 2, 4 in the same order and only moves the brackets. Only the second option does this; the others change the numbers themselves. (Book MCQ Q3(ii).)

mcqs.q: Which one illustrates the Associative Law of multiplication?
mcqs.why: The numbers 4, 3, 6 stay in order and only the grouping changes from (3 x 6) to (4 x 3). Both sides equal 72. The other options alter the numbers. (Book MCQ Q3(iii).)
