lessons.title: Exercise 2.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In the radical n-th root of a, n is the index and a is the radicand; if no index is written, the index is 2.
  • Conversion: n-th root of a = a^(1/n), and more generally the n-th root of a^m = a^(m/n).
  • Conversely a^(1/n) is the n-th root of a and a^(m/n) is the n-th root of a^m.
  • Product rule: the n-th root of (ab) = (n-th root of a)(n-th root of b); quotient rule: the n-th root of (a/b) = (n-th root of a)/(n-th root of b).
  • The n-th root of a^n = a; e.g. cube root of 8 = 2 and cube root of 27 = 3.
  • Simplification takes perfect powers out of the radical, e.g. 6 sqrt(18) = 18 sqrt(2) and cube root of (54 x^3 y^3 z^2) = 3xy cube-root(2 z^2).

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Write down the index and radicand for √(11/y).

Ans: Rule: In ⁿ√a, n is the index and a is the radicand; if no index is written, the index is 2.
Here no index is written, so the index is 2.
The quantity under the radical sign is 11/y.
Answer: Index = 2, Radicand = 11/y

Q: Q1(ii). Write down the index and radicand for ∛(13/(3x)).

Ans: Rule: In ⁿ√a, n is the index and a is the radicand.
Here the number written on the radical is 3.
The quantity under the radical sign is 13/(3x).
Answer: Index = 3, Radicand = 13/(3x)

Q: Q1(iii). Write down the index and radicand for ⁵√(ab²).

Ans: Rule: In ⁿ√a, n is the index and a is the radicand.
Here the number written on the radical is 5.
The quantity under the radical sign is ab².
Answer: Index = 5, Radicand = ab²

Q: Q2(i). Transform into exponential form (do not simplify): √36

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√a = a^(1/n); for a square root, √a = a^(1/2).
√36 = (36)^(1/2)
Answer: (36)^(1/2)

Q: Q2(ii). Transform into exponential form (do not simplify): √1000

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√a = a^(1/n); for a square root, √a = a^(1/2).
√1000 = (1000)^(1/2)
Answer: (1000)^(1/2)

Q: Q2(iii). Transform into exponential form (do not simplify): ∛8

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√a = a^(1/n); for a cube root, ∛a = a^(1/3).
∛8 = (8)^(1/3)
Answer: (8)^(1/3)

Q: Q2(iv). Transform into exponential form (do not simplify): ⁿ√q

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√a = a^(1/n).
ⁿ√q = (q)^(1/n)
Answer: (q)^(1/n)

Q: Q2(v). Transform into exponential form (do not simplify): √((5 - 6a²)³)

Ans: Rule: a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(a^m), so ⁿ√(a^m) = a^(m/n).
Here the index is 2 and the power of the radicand is 3.
√((5 - 6a²)³) = (5 - 6a²)^(3/2)
Answer: (5 - 6a²)^(3/2)

Q: Q2(vi). Transform into exponential form (do not simplify): ∛(-64)

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√a = a^(1/n); for a cube root, ∛a = a^(1/3).
∛(-64) = (-64)^(1/3)
Answer: (-64)^(1/3)

Q: Q3(i). Transform into radical form: -7^(1/3)

Ans: Rule: a^(1/n) = ⁿ√a, and a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(a^m).
7^(1/3) = ∛7
The minus sign stays outside the radical.
-7^(1/3) = -∛7
Answer: -∛7

Q: Q3(ii). Transform into radical form: x^(-3/2)

Ans: Rule: a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(a^m); a negative exponent gives a reciprocal, x^(-3/2) = 1/(x^(3/2)).
x^(3/2) = √(x³)
So x^(-3/2) = 1/√(x³), written in radical form as √(x^(-3)).
Answer: √(x^(-3))

Q: Q3(iii). Transform into radical form: (-8)^(1/5)

Ans: Rule: a^(1/n) = ⁿ√a.
(-8)^(1/5) = ⁵√(-8)
Answer: ⁵√(-8)

Q: Q3(iv). Transform into radical form: y^(3/4)

Ans: Rule: a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(a^m).
Here m = 3 and n = 4.
y^(3/4) = ⁴√(y³)
Answer: ⁴√(y³)

Q: Q3(v). Transform into radical form: b^(4/5)

Ans: Rule: a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(a^m).
Here m = 4 and n = 5.
b^(4/5) = ⁵√(b⁴)
Answer: ⁵√(b⁴)

Q: Q3(vi). Transform into radical form: (3x)^(1/q)

Ans: Rule: a^(1/n) = ⁿ√a.
Here the base is 3x and the index is q.
(3x)^(1/q) = ᵠ√(3x)
Answer: ᵠ√(3x) (the q-th root of 3x)

Q: Q4(i). Simplify: ∛(125x)

Ans: Rule: Product rule of radicals: ⁿ√(ab) = ⁿ√a × ⁿ√b, and ⁿ√(a^n) = a.
∛(125x) = ∛125 × ∛x
125 = 5³, so ∛125 = 5.
= 5 × ∛x
Answer: 5∛x

Q: Q4(ii). Simplify: ∛(8/27)

Ans: Rule: Quotient rule of radicals: ⁿ√(a/b) = ⁿ√a / ⁿ√b, and ⁿ√(a^n) = a.
∛(8/27) = ∛8 / ∛27
8 = 2³, so ∛8 = 2.
27 = 3³, so ∛27 = 3.
= 2/3
Answer: 2/3

Q: Q4(iii). Simplify: √((625x³y⁴)/(25xy²))

Ans: Rule: Quotient rule of radicals: √(a/b) = √a / √b; divide the radicands first, then take perfect squares out.
(625x³y⁴)/(25xy²) = 25x²y²
√(25x²y²) = √25 × √(x²) × √(y²)
= 5 × x × y
Answer: 5xy

Q: Q4(iv). Simplify: √((3y - 5)²)

Ans: Rule: √(a²) = a (the principal, positive root; here the expression itself is taken).
√((3y - 5)²) = 3y - 5
Answer: 3y - 5

Q: Q4(v). Simplify: 6√18

Ans: Rule: Product rule of radicals: √(ab) = √a × √b; write the radicand as a perfect square times the remaining factor.
18 = 9 × 2
6√18 = 6 × √9 × √2
= 6 × 3 × √2
= 18√2
Answer: 18√2

Q: Q4(vi). Simplify: ∛(54x³y³z²)

Ans: Rule: Product rule of radicals: ⁿ√(ab) = ⁿ√a × ⁿ√b, and ⁿ√(a^n) = a.
54 = 27 × 2 = 3³ × 2
∛(54x³y³z²) = ∛(3³ × 2 × x³ × y³ × z²)
= ∛(3³) × ∛(x³) × ∛(y³) × ∛(2z²)
= 3 × x × y × ∛(2z²)
Answer: 3xy∛(2z²)

mcqs.q: For the radical sqrt(11/y) (no index written), the index and radicand are:
mcqs.why: In n-th root notation, n is the index and the quantity under the sign is the radicand. No index is written, so the index is understood to be 2 (square root). The radicand is everything under the sign: 11/y.

mcqs.q: For the cube root of 13/(3x), the index and radicand are:
mcqs.why: The small number written on the radical is 3, so the index is 3 (cube root). The quantity under the radical sign, 13/(3x), is the radicand.

mcqs.q: The exponential form of sqrt(36) (do not simplify) is:
mcqs.why: Rule: the n-th root of a = a^(1/n). A square root has index 2, so sqrt(36) = 36^(1/2). The instruction says do not simplify, so we stop here (its value would be 6).

mcqs.q: The exponential form of the cube root of 8 is:
mcqs.why: Rule: the n-th root of a = a^(1/n). A cube root has index 3, so cube-root(8) = 8^(1/3). (Its value is 2, but the question asks only for the form.)

mcqs.q: The exponential form of sqrt((5 - 6a^2)^3) is:
mcqs.why: Rule: the n-th root of (base^m) = base^(m/n). Here the index is 2 (square root) and the radicand's power is m = 3, so the exponent is 3/2: (5 - 6a^2)^(3/2).

mcqs.q: The radical form of y^(3/4) is:
mcqs.why: Rule: a^(m/n) = n-th root of (a^m). Here m = 3 (numerator, the power) and n = 4 (denominator, the index). So y^(3/4) = fourth root of (y^3).

mcqs.q: The radical form of -7^(1/3) is:
mcqs.why: 7^(1/3) = cube root of 7 by a^(1/n) = n-th root of a. The minus sign is outside the power, so it stays outside the radical: -7^(1/3) = -(cube root of 7).

mcqs.q: The radical form of (-8)^(1/5) is:
mcqs.why: Rule: a^(1/n) = n-th root of a. Here a = -8 (the whole bracket is the base) and n = 5, so (-8)^(1/5) = fifth root of (-8). The negative stays inside because it is part of the base.

mcqs.q: Simplify: cube root of (125x).
mcqs.why: Product rule: cube-root(125x) = cube-root(125) x cube-root(x). Since 125 = 5^3, cube-root(125) = 5. Result: 5 x cube-root(x) = 5 cube-root(x).

mcqs.q: Simplify: cube root of (8/27).
mcqs.why: Quotient rule: cube-root(8/27) = cube-root(8)/cube-root(27). Since 8 = 2^3, cube-root(8) = 2; since 27 = 3^3, cube-root(27) = 3. Result: 2/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify: sqrt((625 x^3 y^4)/(25 x y^2)).
mcqs.why: Step 1: divide inside: (625/25) = 25, x^3/x = x^2, y^4/y^2 = y^2, giving sqrt(25 x^2 y^2). Step 2: sqrt(25) = 5, sqrt(x^2) = x, sqrt(y^2) = y. Result: 5xy.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 6 sqrt(18).
mcqs.why: Write 18 = 9 x 2 with 9 a perfect square. 6 sqrt(18) = 6 x sqrt(9) x sqrt(2) = 6 x 3 x sqrt(2) = 18 sqrt(2).

mcqs.q: Simplify: cube root of (54 x^3 y^3 z^2).
options: 3 cube root of (2 x y z)
mcqs.why: Write 54 = 27 x 2 = 3^3 x 2. Take cube roots factor by factor: cube-root(3^3) = 3, cube-root(x^3) = x, cube-root(y^3) = y, and 2z^2 has no cube factor so it stays inside. Result: 3xy cube-root(2z^2).

mcqs.q: Simplify: sqrt((3y - 5)^2).
mcqs.why: Rule: sqrt(a^2) = a (the principal root, here the expression itself). With a = 3y - 5, sqrt((3y-5)^2) = 3y - 5.

mcqs.q: The exponential form of the n-th root of q is:
mcqs.why: General rule: the n-th root of a = a^(1/n) for any index n. Replacing a by q gives: n-th root of q = q^(1/n).

lessons.title: Exercise 2.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In a^n, a is the base and n is the exponent (index); a^n itself is the value. A negative exponent gives a reciprocal: a^(-n) = 1/a^n, e.g. 2^(-9) = 1/512.
  • Multiplication law: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n). Division law: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n).
  • Power law: (a^m)^n = a^(mn); also (ab)^n = a^n b^n and (a/b)^n = a^n / b^n.
  • Zero index: a^0 = 1 for a not 0.
  • An even power of a negative base is positive and an odd power is negative: (-4)^2 = 16, (-a)^7 = -a^7.
  • Complicated expressions are simplified by writing every base in prime factors and applying the laws, e.g. the proof expression simplifies to 2^2 = 4 and then (4)^(1/2) = 2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Write the base, exponent and value: (2)^(-9) = 1/512

Ans: Rule: In a^n, a is the base, n is the exponent and a^n itself is the value; a^(-n) = 1/(a^n).
Here the power is written on 2.
The power is -9.
Value: 2^(-9) = 1/(2^9) = 1/512.
Answer: Base = 2, Exponent = -9, Value = 1/512
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is Base = 2, Exponent = -9, Value = 1/512. The printed key gives the value as 1/1024.

Q: Q1(ii). Write the base, exponent and value: (a/b)^p = (a^p)/(b^p)

Ans: Rule: In a^n, a is the base and n is the exponent; (a/b)^n = (a^n)/(b^n).
Here the power p is written on the fraction a/b as a whole.
So the base is a/b and the exponent is p.
Value: (a/b)^p = (a^p)/(b^p).
Answer: Base = a/b, Exponent = p, Value = (a^p)/(b^p)

Q: Q1(iii). Write the base, exponent and value: (-4)² = 16

Ans: Rule: In a^n, a is the base, n is the exponent and a^n itself is the value.
Here the power 2 is written on -4.
Value: (-4)² = (-4) × (-4) = 16.
Answer: Base = -4, Exponent = 2, Value = 16
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is Base = -4, Exponent = 2, Value = 16. The printed key gives the exponent as 21.

Q: Q2(i). Simplify: a³ × a⁵

Ans: Rule: Multiplication law of indices: a^m × a^n = a^(m + n).
a³ × a⁵ = a^(3 + 5)
= a^8
Answer: a^8

Q: Q2(ii). Simplify: (b/a)^(3/2) × (b/a)^(-2/3)

Ans: Rule: Multiplication law of indices: a^m × a^n = a^(m + n).
(b/a)^(3/2) × (b/a)^(-2/3) = (b/a)^(3/2 - 2/3)
3/2 - 2/3 = 9/6 - 4/6 = 5/6
= (b/a)^(5/6)
Answer: (b/a)^(5/6)

Q: Q2(iii). Simplify: (-a)⁴ × (-a)³

Ans: Rule: Multiplication law of indices: a^m × a^n = a^(m + n).
(-a)⁴ × (-a)³ = (-a)^(4 + 3)
= (-a)^7
An odd power of a negative quantity is negative: (-a)^7 = -a^7.
Answer: -a^7

Q: Q2(iv). Simplify: (-2a²b³)³

Ans: Rule: (ab)^n = a^n b^n and power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
(-2a²b³)³ = (-2)³ × (a²)³ × (b³)³
= -8 × a^6 × b^9
Answer: -8a^6b^9

Q: Q2(v). Simplify: a³(-2b)²

Ans: Rule: (ab)^n = a^n b^n.
(-2b)² = (-2)² × b² = 4b²
a³ × 4b² = 4a³b²
Answer: 4a³b²

Q: Q2(vi). Simplify: (a²b)(a²b)

Ans: Rule: Multiplication law of indices: a^m × a^n = a^(m + n), applied to each letter separately.
(a²b)(a²b) = a^(2 + 2) × b^(1 + 1)
= a⁴b²
Answer: a⁴b²

Q: Q2(vii). Simplify: (a⁰b⁰)/2

Ans: Rule: Zero index: a⁰ = 1 for a ≠ 0.
a⁰ = 1 and b⁰ = 1.
(a⁰b⁰)/2 = (1 × 1)/2
= 1/2
Answer: 1/2

Q: Q2(viii). Simplify: (-3a²b²)²

Ans: Rule: (ab)^n = a^n b^n and power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
(-3a²b²)² = (-3)² × (a²)² × (b²)²
= 9 × a⁴ × b⁴
Answer: 9a⁴b⁴

Q: Q2(ix). Simplify: ((a²)/(b⁴))^(3/2)

Ans: Rule: (a/b)^n = (a^n)/(b^n) and power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
((a²)/(b⁴))^(3/2) = (a²)^(3/2) / (b⁴)^(3/2)
= a³ / b^6
= a³b^(-6)
Answer: a³b^(-6)

Q: Q3(i). Simplify: (7^6)/(7^4)

Ans: Rule: Division law of indices: (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n).
(7^6)/(7^4) = 7^(6 - 4)
= 7²
Answer: 7² (= 49)

Q: Q3(ii). Simplify: (2⁴ × 5³)/(10²)

Ans: Rule: (ab)^n = a^n b^n, so 10² = 2² × 5²; then use the division law (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n).
(2⁴ × 5³)/(10²) = (2⁴ × 5³)/(2² × 5²)
= 2^(4 - 2) × 5^(3 - 2)
= 2² × 5¹
= 4 × 5
= 20
Answer: 20

Q: Q3(iii). Simplify: { ((a + b)² × (c + d)³) / ((a + b) × (c + d)²) }³

Ans: Rule: Division law of indices: (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n), then power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
Inside the bracket: (a + b)^(2 - 1) × (c + d)^(3 - 2) = (a + b) × (c + d).
Now raise to the power 3: ((a + b)(c + d))³
= (a + b)³(c + d)³
Answer: (a + b)³(c + d)³

Q: Q3(iv). Simplify: (∛a)^(1/2)

Ans: Rule: ∛a = a^(1/3), and power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
(∛a)^(1/2) = (a^(1/3))^(1/2)
= a^(1/3 × 1/2)
= a^(1/6)
Answer: a^(1/6)

Q: Q3(v). Simplify: ⁵√(x⁵) × ⁴√(x⁴)

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√(a^n) = a.
⁵√(x⁵) = x
⁴√(x⁴) = x
x × x = x²
Answer: x²

Q: Q4(i). Simplify so that the answer contains no fractional or negative exponents: (25/81)^(1/2)

Ans: Rule: (a/b)^(1/2) = √(a/b) = √a/√b; a fractional exponent 1/2 means square root.
(25/81)^(1/2) = √25/√81
√25 = 5 and √81 = 9.
= 5/9
Answer: 5/9

Q: Q4(ii). Simplify so that the answer contains no fractional or negative exponents: (ab)^(1/b) / (1/(ab))^(1/a)

Ans: Rule: Negative index: (1/x)^n in the denominator — first use (1/(ab))^(1/a) = (ab)^(-1/a), and division law (x^m)/(x^n) = x^(m - n); then (xy)^n = x^n y^n.
(ab)^(1/b) / (1/(ab))^(1/a) = (ab)^(1/b) / (ab)^(-1/a)
= (ab)^(1/b + 1/a)
1/b + 1/a = (a + b)/(ab)
= (ab)^((a + b)/(ab))
= a^((a + b)/(ab)) × b^((a + b)/(ab))
In radical form this is the (ab)-th root of (ab)^(a + b), with no negative exponent.
Answer: a^((a + b)/(ab)) · b^((a + b)/(ab))

Q: Q4(iii). Simplify so that the answer contains no fractional or negative exponents: (2^(p + 1) × 3^(2p - q) × 5^(p + q) × 6^q) / (6^p × 10^(q + 2) × 15^p)

Ans: Rule: Write every composite base in prime factors, (ab)^n = a^n b^n, then use a^m × a^n = a^(m + n) and (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n).
6^q = 2^q × 3^q, so the numerator = 2^(p + 1 + q) × 3^(2p - q + q) × 5^(p + q) = 2^(p + q + 1) × 3^(2p) × 5^(p + q).
6^p = 2^p × 3^p, 10^(q + 2) = 2^(q + 2) × 5^(q + 2), 15^p = 3^p × 5^p, so the denominator = 2^(p + q + 2) × 3^(2p) × 5^(p + q + 2).
Divide: 2^((p + q + 1) - (p + q + 2)) × 3^(2p - 2p) × 5^((p + q) - (p + q + 2))
= 2^(-1) × 3^0 × 5^(-2)
= 1/(2 × 25)
= 1/50
Answer: 1/50

Q: Q4(iv). Simplify so that the answer contains no fractional or negative exponents: (x^p/x^q)^(p + q) × (x^q/x^r)^(q + r) × (x^r/x^p)^(r + p)

Ans: Rule: Division law (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n), power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn), and a^m × a^n = a^(m + n).
(x^p/x^q)^(p + q) = (x^(p - q))^(p + q) = x^(p² - q²)
(x^q/x^r)^(q + r) = x^(q² - r²)
(x^r/x^p)^(r + p) = x^(r² - p²)
Multiply: x^((p² - q²) + (q² - r²) + (r² - p²))
The exponent is p² - q² + q² - r² + r² - p² = 0.
= x^0
= 1 (zero index: x⁰ = 1)
Answer: 1

Q: Q5. Prove that ((4⁵ × 64³ × 2³) / (8⁵ × (128)²))^(1/2) = 2.

Ans: Given:
LHS = ((4⁵ × 64³ × 2³) / (8⁵ × (128)²))^(1/2)
To Prove:
LHS = 2
Proof:
Rule: Write every base as a power of 2, then use a^m × a^n = a^(m + n), (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n) and (a^m)^n = a^(mn).
4⁵ = (2²)⁵ = 2^10
64³ = (2^6)³ = 2^18
Numerator = 2^10 × 2^18 × 2³ = 2^(10 + 18 + 3) = 2^31
8⁵ = (2³)⁵ = 2^15
(128)² = (2^7)² = 2^14
Denominator = 2^15 × 2^14 = 2^(15 + 14) = 2^29
Fraction = 2^(31 - 29) = 2² = 4
LHS = (4)^(1/2) = 2
= RHS
Hence proved.

mcqs.q: In (2)^(-9) = 1/512, the base, exponent and value are:
mcqs.why: The power -9 is written on 2, so base = 2 and exponent = -9. Value: 2^(-9) = 1/2^9 = 1/512 since 2^9 = 512. The book key wrongly gives the value as 1/1024.

mcqs.q: In (-4)^2 = 16, the base and exponent are:
mcqs.why: The power 2 is written on the bracket (-4), so the base is -4 (including its sign) and the exponent is 2. Value: (-4)x(-4) = 16. The book key wrongly gives the exponent as 21.

mcqs.q: Simplify: a^3 x a^5.
mcqs.why: Multiplication law: a^m x a^n = a^(m+n). So a^3 x a^5 = a^(3+5) = a^8. Add the exponents; do not multiply them.
Same base, so add exponents: 3/2 + (-2/3) = 3/2 - 2/3 = 9/6 - 4/6 = 5/6. Result: (b/a)^(5/6).

mcqs.q: Simplify: (-2a^2 b^3)^3.
mcqs.why: Raise each factor to power 3: (-2)^3 = -8; (a^2)^3 = a^(2x3) = a^6 by the power law; (b^3)^3 = b^9. Multiply: -8 a^6 b^9.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (a^0 b^0)/2.
mcqs.why: Zero index: a^0 = 1 and b^0 = 1 (for non-zero a, b). So (a^0 b^0)/2 = (1 x 1)/2 = 1/2.
Division law: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n). So 7^6 / 7^4 = 7^(6-4) = 7^2 = 49. Subtract the exponents when dividing the same base.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (cube root of a)^(1/2).
mcqs.why: Step 1: cube root of a = a^(1/3). Step 2: power law (a^m)^n = a^(mn): (a^(1/3))^(1/2) = a^(1/3 x 1/2) = a^(1/6).

mcqs.q: Simplify: (25/81)^(1/2) with no fractional exponent.
mcqs.why: Exponent 1/2 means square root: (25/81)^(1/2) = sqrt(25)/sqrt(81). sqrt(25) = 5 and sqrt(81) = 9, giving 5/9.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (-a)^4 x (-a)^3.
mcqs.why: Add exponents (same base): (-a)^(4+3) = (-a)^7. An odd power (7) of a negative quantity is negative, so (-a)^7 = -a^7.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 5th root of (x^5) x 4th root of (x^4).
mcqs.why: Rule: n-th root of (a^n) = a. So 5th-root(x^5) = x and 4th-root(x^4) = x. Multiply: x times x = x^2.
Apply the power to numerator and denominator: (a^2)^(3/2) = a^(2 x 3/2) = a^3; (b^4)^(3/2) = b^(4 x 3/2) = b^6. So the value is a^3 / b^6 = a^3 b^(-6).

mcqs.q: The expression ((4^5 x 64^3 x 2^3)/(8^5 x 128^2))^(1/2) equals:
mcqs.why: Write all as powers of 2: numerator = 2^10 x 2^18 x 2^3 = 2^31; denominator = 2^15 x 2^14 = 2^29. Fraction = 2^(31-29) = 2^2 = 4. Then (4)^(1/2) = 2. Hence the value is 2, as the exercise proves.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (x^p/x^q)^(p+q) x (x^q/x^r)^(q+r) x (x^r/x^p)^(r+p).
mcqs.why: Each factor: (x^(p-q))^(p+q) = x^(p^2 - q^2); similarly x^(q^2 - r^2) and x^(r^2 - p^2). Total exponent = (p^2-q^2)+(q^2-r^2)+(r^2-p^2) = 0. So the value is x^0 = 1 by the zero index law.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A complex number has the form a + bi where i = sqrt(-1) and i^2 = -1; a is the real part and b the imaginary part.
  • Addition and subtraction: (a + bi) +/- (c + di) = (a +/- c) + (b +/- d)i — combine real parts and imaginary parts separately.
  • Multiplication: (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i, using i^2 = -1.
  • Division: multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, e.g. (2 + i)/(5 - i) = 9/26 + 7/26 i.
  • The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi: keep the real part and change the sign of the imaginary part.
  • A difference such as (6 + 7i) - (6 - 7i) = 14i can be purely imaginary, and (9 - 8i) - (9 + 4i) = -12i.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Add the complex numbers: 8 + 9i, 5 + 2i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i — add real parts and imaginary parts separately.
(8 + 9i) + (5 + 2i) = (8 + 5) + (9 + 2)i
= 13 + 11i
Answer: 13 + 11i

Q: Q1(ii). Add the complex numbers: 6 + 3i, 3 - 5i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i — add real parts and imaginary parts separately.
(6 + 3i) + (3 - 5i) = (6 + 3) + (3 - 5)i
= 9 - 2i
Answer: 9 - 2i

Q: Q1(iii). Add the complex numbers: 2i + 3, 8 - 5√(-1)

Ans: Rule: i = √(-1), and (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i.
Write both in the form a + bi: 3 + 2i and 8 - 5i.
(3 + 2i) + (8 - 5i) = (3 + 8) + (2 - 5)i
= 11 - 3i
Answer: 11 - 3i

Q: Q1(iv). Add the complex numbers: √3 + √2 i, 3√3 - 2√2 i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i — add real parts and imaginary parts separately.
(√3 + √2 i) + (3√3 - 2√2 i) = (√3 + 3√3) + (√2 - 2√2)i
= 4√3 - √2 i
Answer: 4√3 - √2 i
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 4√3 - √2 i. The printed key gives -8.

Q: Q2(i). Subtract: -2 + 3i from 6 - 3i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) - (c + di) = (a - c) + (b - d)i — subtract real parts and imaginary parts separately.
(6 - 3i) - (-2 + 3i) = 6 - 3i + 2 - 3i
= (6 + 2) + (-3 - 3)i
= 8 - 6i
Answer: 8 - 6i

Q: Q2(ii). Subtract: 9 + 4i from 9 - 8i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) - (c + di) = (a - c) + (b - d)i.
(9 - 8i) - (9 + 4i) = 9 - 8i - 9 - 4i
= (9 - 9) + (-8 - 4)i
= -12i
Answer: 0 - 12i, i.e. -12i

Q: Q2(iii). Subtract: 1 - 3i from 8 - i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) - (c + di) = (a - c) + (b - d)i.
(8 - i) - (1 - 3i) = 8 - i - 1 + 3i
= (8 - 1) + (-1 + 3)i
= 7 + 2i
Answer: 7 + 2i

Q: Q2(iv). Subtract: 6 - 7i from 6 + 7i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) - (c + di) = (a - c) + (b - d)i.
(6 + 7i) - (6 - 7i) = 6 + 7i - 6 + 7i
= (6 - 6) + (7 + 7)i
= 14i
Answer: 0 + 14i, i.e. 14i

Q: Q3(i). Multiply the complex numbers: 1 + 2i, 3 - 8i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i, using i² = -1.
(1 + 2i)(3 - 8i) = 1 × 3 + 1 × (-8i) + 2i × 3 + 2i × (-8i)
= 3 - 8i + 6i - 16i²
= 3 - 2i - 16(-1)
= 3 - 2i + 16
= 19 - 2i
Answer: 19 - 2i

Q: Q3(ii). Multiply the complex numbers: 2i, 4 - 7i

Ans: Rule: Multiply term by term and use i² = -1.
(2i)(4 - 7i) = 2i × 4 + 2i × (-7i)
= 8i - 14i²
= 8i - 14(-1)
= 14 + 8i
Answer: 14 + 8i

Q: Q3(iii). Multiply the complex numbers: 5 - 3i, 2 - 4i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i, using i² = -1.
(5 - 3i)(2 - 4i) = 5 × 2 + 5 × (-4i) + (-3i) × 2 + (-3i)(-4i)
= 10 - 20i - 6i + 12i²
= 10 - 26i + 12(-1)
= 10 - 26i - 12
= -2 - 26i
Answer: -2 - 26i

Q: Q3(iv). Multiply the complex numbers: √2 + i, 1 - √2 i

Ans: Rule: (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i, using i² = -1.
(√2 + i)(1 - √2 i) = √2 × 1 + √2 × (-√2 i) + i × 1 + i × (-√2 i)
= √2 - 2i + i - √2 i²
= √2 - i - √2(-1)
= √2 - i + √2
= 2√2 - i
Answer: 2√2 - i

Q: Q4(i). Divide the first complex number by the second: Z₁ = 2 + i, Z₂ = 5 - i

Ans: Rule: To divide, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator (rationalization), and use i² = -1. Conjugate of 5 - i is 5 + i.
(2 + i)/(5 - i) = (2 + i)(5 + i) / (5 - i)(5 + i)
Numerator: (2 + i)(5 + i) = 10 + 2i + 5i + i² = 10 + 7i - 1 = 9 + 7i
Denominator: (5 - i)(5 + i) = 25 - i² = 25 + 1 = 26
= (9 + 7i)/26
= 9/26 + 7/26 i
Answer: 9/26 + 7/26 i

Q: Q4(ii). Divide the first complex number by the second: Z₁ = 3i + 4, Z₂ = 1 - i

Ans: Rule: To divide, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator (rationalization), and use i² = -1. Conjugate of 1 - i is 1 + i.
(4 + 3i)/(1 - i) = (4 + 3i)(1 + i) / (1 - i)(1 + i)
Numerator: (4 + 3i)(1 + i) = 4 + 4i + 3i + 3i² = 4 + 7i - 3 = 1 + 7i
Denominator: (1 - i)(1 + i) = 1 - i² = 1 + 1 = 2
= (1 + 7i)/2
= 1/2 + 7/2 i
Answer: 1/2 + 7/2 i

Q: Q5(i). Perform the operation and reduce to the form a + bi: (4 - 3i) + (2 - 3i)

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) + (c + di) = (a + c) + (b + d)i.
(4 - 3i) + (2 - 3i) = (4 + 2) + (-3 - 3)i
= 6 - 6i
Answer: 6 - 6i

Q: Q5(ii). Perform the operation and reduce to the form a + bi: (5 - 2i) - (4 - 7i)

Ans: Rule: (a + bi) - (c + di) = (a - c) + (b - d)i.
(5 - 2i) - (4 - 7i) = 5 - 2i - 4 + 7i
= (5 - 4) + (-2 + 7)i
= 1 + 5i
Answer: 1 + 5i

Q: Q5(iii). Perform the operation and reduce to the form a + bi: 2i(4 - 5i)

Ans: Rule: Multiply term by term and use i² = -1.
2i(4 - 5i) = 2i × 4 + 2i × (-5i)
= 8i - 10i²
= 8i - 10(-1)
= 10 + 8i
Answer: 10 + 8i

Q: Q5(iv). Perform the operation and reduce to the form a + bi: (2 - 3i) ÷ (4 - 5i)

Ans: Rule: To divide, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator (rationalization), and use i² = -1. Conjugate of 4 - 5i is 4 + 5i.
(2 - 3i)/(4 - 5i) = (2 - 3i)(4 + 5i) / (4 - 5i)(4 + 5i)
Numerator: (2 - 3i)(4 + 5i) = 8 + 10i - 12i - 15i² = 8 - 2i + 15 = 23 - 2i
Denominator: (4 - 5i)(4 + 5i) = 16 - 25i² = 16 + 25 = 41
= (23 - 2i)/41
= 23/41 - 2/41 i
Answer: 23/41 - 2/41 i

Q: Q6(i). Find the complex conjugate of -8 - 3i.

Ans: Rule: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi — keep the real part, change the sign of the imaginary part.
Conjugate of -8 - 3i = -8 + 3i
Answer: -8 + 3i

Q: Q6(ii). Find the complex conjugate of -4 + 9i.

Ans: Rule: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi — keep the real part, change the sign of the imaginary part.
Conjugate of -4 + 9i = -4 - 9i
Answer: -4 - 9i

Q: Q6(iii). Find the complex conjugate of 7 + 6i.

Ans: Rule: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi — keep the real part, change the sign of the imaginary part.
Conjugate of 7 + 6i = 7 - 6i
Answer: 7 - 6i

Q: Q6(iv). Find the complex conjugate of √5 - i.

Ans: Rule: The conjugate of a + bi is a - bi — keep the real part, change the sign of the imaginary part.
√5 - i = √5 + (-1)i, so its conjugate is √5 + i.
Answer: √5 + i

mcqs.why: Add real parts: 8 + 5 = 13. Add imaginary parts: 9 + 2 = 11. Result: 13 + 11i, using (a+bi)+(c+di) = (a+c)+(b+d)i.
Real parts: 6 + 3 = 9. Imaginary parts: 3 + (-5) = -2. Result: 9 - 2i.

mcqs.q: Add: (sqrt(3) + sqrt(2) i) + (3 sqrt(3) - 2 sqrt(2) i).
mcqs.why: Real parts: sqrt(3) + 3sqrt(3) = 4sqrt(3). Imaginary parts: sqrt(2) - 2sqrt(2) = -sqrt(2). Result: 4sqrt(3) - sqrt(2) i. The book key wrongly gives -8 for this sum.
Remove brackets: 6 - 3i + 2 - 3i. Real parts: 6 + 2 = 8. Imaginary parts: -3 - 3 = -6. Result: 8 - 6i.

mcqs.q: Subtract (9 + 4i) from (9 - 8i): (9 - 8i) - (9 + 4i).
mcqs.why: Compute: 9 - 8i - 9 - 4i. Real parts: 9 - 9 = 0. Imaginary parts: -8 - 4 = -12. Result: -12i, a purely imaginary number.

mcqs.q: Multiply: (1 + 2i)(3 - 8i).
Multiply: (2i)(4 - 7i).
Multiply: (5 - 3i)(2 - 4i).
mcqs.why: Expand: 10 - 20i - 6i + 12i^2 = 10 - 26i + 12(-1) = 10 - 26i - 12 = -2 - 26i, using i^2 = -1 and formula (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i with ac - bd = 10 - 12 = -2.

mcqs.q: Divide: (2 + i)/(5 - i).
mcqs.why: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 5 + i. Numerator: (2+i)(5+i) = 10 + 7i + i^2 = 9 + 7i. Denominator: (5-i)(5+i) = 25 - i^2 = 26. Result: (9 + 7i)/26 = 9/26 + 7/26 i.

mcqs.q: Divide: (4 + 3i)/(1 - i).
mcqs.why: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 1 + i. Numerator: (4+3i)(1+i) = 4 + 7i + 3i^2 = 1 + 7i. Denominator: (1-i)(1+i) = 1 - i^2 = 2. Result: (1 + 7i)/2 = 1/2 + 7/2 i.

mcqs.q: Simplify: (5 - 2i) - (4 - 7i).
mcqs.why: Compute: 5 - 2i - 4 + 7i. Real parts: 5 - 4 = 1. Imaginary parts: -2 + 7 = 5. Result: 1 + 5i.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 2i(4 - 5i).

mcqs.why: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate 4 + 5i. Numerator: (2-3i)(4+5i) = 8 - 2i - 15i^2 = 23 - 2i. Denominator: (4-5i)(4+5i) = 16 - 25i^2 = 41. Result: (23 - 2i)/41 = 23/41 - 2/41 i.

mcqs.q: The complex conjugate of -8 - 3i is:
mcqs.why: Conjugate of a + bi is a - bi: keep the real part (-8) and reverse the sign of the imaginary part (-3 becomes +3). So the conjugate of -8 - 3i is -8 + 3i.

mcqs.q: The complex conjugate of sqrt(5) - i is:
mcqs.why: Write sqrt(5) - i as sqrt(5) + (-1)i, so a = sqrt(5), b = -1. The conjugate a - bi = sqrt(5) + 1i = sqrt(5) + i: only the imaginary sign changes.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Conversions: 3^(1/3) = cube root of 3 (not sqrt(3)); 2^(2/3) = cube root of 4; sqrt(49) = 7; cube root of 27 = 3.
  • The additive inverse of sqrt(5) is -sqrt(5); the multiplicative identity of real numbers is 1.
  • i = sqrt(-1), i^2 = -1; hence sqrt(-1) x sqrt(-1) = -1 and (i)(-i) = 1.
  • 0 is neither positive nor negative; sqrt(0) = 0.
  • Numbers greater than -3 but less than 6 are written {x : -3 < x < 6}.
  • Simplifications in the review use radical and exponent laws, e.g. -3 sqrt(48) = -12 sqrt(3), (8i)(-8i) = 64, and the final exponent expression simplifies to 12.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Tell whether the following is true or false: 3^(1/3) = √3

Ans: Rule: a^(1/n) = ⁿ√a, so 3^(1/3) = ∛3, not √3.
∛3 ≈ 1.442, while √3 ≈ 1.732.
They are not equal.
Answer: False

Q: Q1(ii). Tell whether the following is true or false: 2^(2/3) = ∛4

Ans: Rule: a^(m/n) = ⁿ√(a^m).
2^(2/3) = ∛(2²)
= ∛4
Both sides are equal.
Answer: True

Q: Q1(iii). Tell whether the following is true or false: √49 = √7

Ans: Rule: √49 is the principal square root of 49.
√49 = 7, because 7² = 49.
√7 ≈ 2.646 ≠ 7.
Answer: False

Q: Q1(iv). Tell whether the following is true or false: ∛27 = x³

Ans: Rule: ⁿ√(a^n) = a, so ∛27 = ∛(3³) = 3.
∛27 = 3, which is not x³ (x is not even defined here).
Answer: False

Q: Q2(i). Select the correct answer: The additive inverse of √5 is

Options: (a) -√5 (b) 1/√5 (c) √(-3) (d) -5

Correct answer: -√5

Q: Q2(ii). Select the correct answer: 2(3 + 4) = 2 × 3 + 2 × 4, here the property used is

Options: (a) Commutative (b) Associative (c) Distributive (d) Closure

Correct answer: Distributive

Q: Q2(iii). Select the correct answer: √(-1) × √(-1) =

Options: (a) 1 (b) i (c) -1 (d) 0

Correct answer: -1

Q: Q2(iv). Select the correct answer: Which of the following represents numbers greater than -3 but less than 6?

Options: (a) {x : -3 > x > 6} (b) {x : -3 ≤ x ≤ 6} (c) {x : -3 < x < 6} (d) {x : -3 ≥ x ≥ 6}

Correct answer: {x : -3 < x < 6}

Q: Q2(v). Select the correct answer: If n = 8 and 16 × 2^m = 4^(n - 8), then m = ?

Options: (a) -4 (b) -2 (c) 0 (d) 8

Correct answer: -4

Q: Q2(vi). Select the correct answer: (i)·(-i) =

Options: (a) 1 (b) -1 (c) -i (d) i

Correct answer: 1

Q: Q2(vii). Select the correct answer: The multiplicative identity of real numbers is

Options: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) -1 (d) R

Correct answer: 1

Q: Q2(viii). Select the correct answer: 0 is

Options: (a) a positive integer (b) a negative integer (c) neither positive nor negative (d) not an integer

Correct answer: neither positive nor negative

Q: Q2(ix). Select the correct answer: For i = √(-1), if 3i(2 + 5i) = x + 6i, then x = ?

Options: (a) 5 (b) -15 (c) 5i (d) 15i

Correct answer: -15

Q: Q2(x). Select the correct answer: √0 =

Options: (a) 0 (b) 1 (c) -1 (d) not defined

Correct answer: 0

Q: Q2(xi). Select the correct answer: √(-(-9)²) = ? (Note: i = √(-1))

Options: (a) 9 (b) 9 + i (c) 9 - i (d) 9i

Correct answer: 9i

Q: Q3(i). Simplify: (-2/3)³

Ans: Rule: (a/b)^n = (a^n)/(b^n); an odd power of a negative number is negative.
(-2/3)³ = (-2)³/(3³)
= -8/27
Answer: -8/27

Q: Q3(ii). Simplify: (-2)³ · (3)²

Ans: Rule: Evaluate each power first, then multiply.
(-2)³ = -8
(3)² = 9
-8 × 9 = -72
Answer: -72

Q: Q3(iii). Simplify: -3√48

Ans: Rule: Product rule of radicals: √(ab) = √a × √b; write the radicand as a perfect square times the remaining factor.
48 = 16 × 3
-3√48 = -3 × √16 × √3
= -3 × 4 × √3
= -12√3
Answer: -12√3

Q: Q3(iv). Simplify: 5/∛9

Ans: Rule: Rationalize the denominator: multiply numerator and denominator by ∛3 so that the denominator becomes ∛27 = 3, using ⁿ√a × ⁿ√b = ⁿ√(ab).
5/∛9 = (5 × ∛3)/(∛9 × ∛3)
= 5∛3/∛27
∛27 = 3.
= 5∛3/3
Answer: 5∛3/3

Q: Q4. Multiply 8i, -8i.

Ans: Rule: Multiply term by term and use i² = -1.
(8i)(-8i) = -64i²
= -64(-1)
= 64
Answer: 64

Q: Q5. Divide 2 - 5i by 1 - 6i.

Ans: Rule: To divide, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator (rationalization), and use i² = -1. Conjugate of 1 - 6i is 1 + 6i.
(2 - 5i)/(1 - 6i) = (2 - 5i)(1 + 6i) / (1 - 6i)(1 + 6i)
Numerator: (2 - 5i)(1 + 6i) = 2 + 12i - 5i - 30i² = 2 + 7i + 30 = 32 + 7i
Denominator: (1 - 6i)(1 + 6i) = 1 - 36i² = 1 + 36 = 37
= (32 + 7i)/37
= 32/37 + 7/37 i
Answer: 32/37 + 7/37 i

Q: Q6. Name the property used: 7 × 1/7 = 1/7 × 7 = 1

Ans: Rule: Multiplicative inverse: a × a⁻¹ = a⁻¹ × a = 1, where a⁻¹ = 1/a.
Here 7 × (1/7) = 1.
So 7 and 1/7 are multiplicative inverses of each other.
Answer: Multiplicative inverse

Q: Q7. Use laws of exponents to simplify: ((81)^n · 3⁵ + (3)^(4n - 1)(243)) / ((9^(2n))(3³))

Ans: Rule: Write every base as a power of 3, then use (a^m)^n = a^(mn), a^m × a^n = a^(m + n) and (a^m)/(a^n) = a^(m - n).
81 = 3⁴, 243 = 3⁵, 9 = 3².
First term of numerator: (3⁴)^n × 3⁵ = 3^(4n) × 3⁵ = 3^(4n + 5).
Second term of numerator: 3^(4n - 1) × 3⁵ = 3^(4n + 4).
Numerator = 3^(4n + 5) + 3^(4n + 4) = 3^(4n + 4)(3 + 1) = 4 × 3^(4n + 4).
Denominator: (3²)^(2n) × 3³ = 3^(4n) × 3³ = 3^(4n + 3).
Divide: 4 × 3^((4n + 4) - (4n + 3)) = 4 × 3¹ = 12.
Check with n = 0: (243 + 243/3)/27 = 324/27 = 12. ✓
Answer: 12
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 12. The printed key gives 6.

mcqs.q: 2^(2/3) equals:
mcqs.why: Rule a^(m/n) = n-th root of (a^m): 2^(2/3) = cube root of (2^2) = cube root of 4. The book's true/false item Q1(ii) is therefore True.

mcqs.q: 3^(1/3) equals:
mcqs.why: Rule a^(1/n) = n-th root of a: 3^(1/3) = cube root of 3, approximately 1.442. It is not sqrt(3), which is approximately 1.732. So the book statement 3^(1/3) = sqrt(3) is False.

mcqs.q: sqrt(-(-9)^2), with i = sqrt(-1), equals:
mcqs.why: Compute inside: (-9)^2 = 81, so -(-9)^2 = -81. Then sqrt(-81) = sqrt(81) x sqrt(-1) = 9i. (Book MCQ Q2(xi), keyed 9i; verified: sqrt of a negative uses i.)

mcqs.q: The additive inverse of sqrt(5) is:
mcqs.why: The additive inverse of a number a is -a, since a + (-a) = 0. For a = sqrt(5), the inverse is -sqrt(5). Note 1/sqrt(5) would be the multiplicative inverse, a different idea. (Book MCQ Q2(i).)

mcqs.q: In 2(3 + 4) = 2 x 3 + 2 x 4, the property used is:
mcqs.why: The factor 2 is multiplied by each term inside the bracket: 2x3 + 2x4. Spreading multiplication over addition is the distributive property. (Book MCQ Q2(ii).)

mcqs.q: sqrt(-1) x sqrt(-1) equals:
mcqs.why: sqrt(-1) = i, so the product is i x i = i^2. By definition i^2 = -1. Hence sqrt(-1) x sqrt(-1) = -1. (Book MCQ Q2(iii).)

mcqs.q: Which set represents numbers greater than -3 but less than 6?
mcqs.why: Greater than -3 means x > -3, written -3 < x; less than 6 means x < 6. Combined with strict inequalities (endpoints excluded): -3 < x < 6. (Book MCQ Q2(iv).)

mcqs.q: If n = 8 and 16 x 2^m = 4^(n - 8), then m equals:
mcqs.why: Substitute n = 8: RHS = 4^(0) = 1. LHS: 16 x 2^m = 2^4 x 2^m = 2^(4+m). Set 2^(4+m) = 1 = 2^0, so 4 + m = 0 and m = -4. (Book MCQ Q2(v), verified by recomputation.)

mcqs.q: (i) x (-i) equals:
mcqs.why: Compute: (i)(-i) = -(i^2) = -(-1) = 1, using i^2 = -1. So (i)(-i) = 1. (Book MCQ Q2(vi).)

mcqs.q: The multiplicative identity of real numbers is:
mcqs.why: The multiplicative identity e satisfies a x e = a for every real a. Only e = 1 works: a x 1 = a. (0 is the additive identity instead.) (Book MCQ Q2(vii).)

mcqs.q: 0 is:
mcqs.why: 0 lies at the origin of the number line: it is not greater than 0 (not positive) and not less than 0 (not negative). It is still an integer and a whole number. (Book MCQ Q2(viii).)

mcqs.q: For i = sqrt(-1), if 3i(2 + 5i) = x + 6i, then x equals:
mcqs.why: Expand LHS: 3i x 2 + 3i x 5i = 6i + 15i^2 = 6i + 15(-1) = -15 + 6i. Compare with x + 6i: the real part gives x = -15. (Book MCQ Q2(ix).)

mcqs.q: sqrt(0) equals:
mcqs.why: sqrt(0) = 0 because 0^2 = 0. Zero has a perfectly defined (principal) square root, namely 0 itself. (Book MCQ Q2(x).)

mcqs.q: Simplify: -3 sqrt(48).
mcqs.why: Write 48 = 16 x 3 with 16 a perfect square. -3 sqrt(48) = -3 x sqrt(16) x sqrt(3) = -3 x 4 x sqrt(3) = -12 sqrt(3).

mcqs.q: Multiply: (8i)(-8i).
mcqs.why: Multiply: (8i)(-8i) = -64 i^2. Use i^2 = -1: -64 x (-1) = 64. The product of the two purely imaginary numbers is the real number 64.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Scientific notation writes a number as x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10.
  • For a number greater than 1, the decimal point is moved left and n is positive; e.g. 405,000 = 4.05 × 10^5.
  • For 0 < x < 1, the decimal point is moved right and n is negative; e.g. 0.00092 = 9.2 × 10^(-4).
  • To return to standard notation, a positive exponent moves the decimal point right and a negative exponent moves it left, filling with zeros.
  • A coefficient that is not yet in scientific form is fixed first, then exponents are added: 0.05 × 10^(-3) = 5 × 10^(-2) × 10^(-3) = 5 × 10^(-5).
  • Division in scientific notation uses (a × 10^m)/(b × 10^n) = (a/b) × 10^(m-n); time = distance/speed gives (9.3 × 10^7)/(1.86 × 10^5) = 5 × 10^2 = 500 seconds.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Write in scientific notation: 405,000

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; move the decimal point left and n is positive.
Move the decimal point 5 places left: 405000 → 4.05
So a = 4.05 and n = 5.
Answer: 4.05 × 10^5

Q: Q1(ii). Write in scientific notation: 1,670,000

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; move the decimal point left and n is positive.
Move the decimal point 6 places left: 1670000 → 1.67
So a = 1.67 and n = 6.
Answer: 1.67 × 10^6

Q: Q1(iii). Write in scientific notation: 0.00000039

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; for 0 < x < 1 move the decimal point right and n is negative.
Move the decimal point 7 places right: 0.00000039 → 3.9
So a = 3.9 and n = -7.
Answer: 3.9 × 10^(-7)

Q: Q1(iv). Write in scientific notation: 0.00092

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; for 0 < x < 1 move the decimal point right and n is negative.
Move the decimal point 4 places right: 0.00092 → 9.2
So a = 9.2 and n = -4.
Answer: 9.2 × 10^(-4)

Q: Q1(v). Write in scientific notation: 234,600,000,000

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; move the decimal point left and n is positive.
Move the decimal point 11 places left: 234600000000 → 2.346
So a = 2.346 and n = 11.
Answer: 2.346 × 10^11

Q: Q1(vi). Write in scientific notation: 8,904,000,000

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; move the decimal point left and n is positive.
Move the decimal point 9 places left: 8904000000 → 8.904
So a = 8.904 and n = 9.
Answer: 8.904 × 10^9

Q: Q1(vii). Write in scientific notation: 0.00104

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; for 0 < x < 1 move the decimal point right and n is negative.
Move the decimal point 3 places right: 0.00104 → 1.04
So a = 1.04 and n = -3.
Answer: 1.04 × 10^(-3)

Q: Q1(viii). Write in scientific notation: 0.00000000514

Ans: Rule: Scientific notation is x = a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10; for 0 < x < 1 move the decimal point right and n is negative.
Move the decimal point 9 places right: 0.00000000514 → 5.14
So a = 5.14 and n = -9.
Answer: 5.14 × 10^(-9)

Q: Q1(ix). Write in scientific notation: 0.05 × 10^(-3)

Ans: Rule: First write the coefficient in scientific notation, then add the exponents using a^m × a^n = a^(m + n).
0.05 = 5 × 10^(-2)
0.05 × 10^(-3) = 5 × 10^(-2) × 10^(-3)
= 5 × 10^(-2 + (-3))
= 5 × 10^(-5)
Answer: 5 × 10^(-5)

Q: Q2(i). Write in standard notation: 8.3 × 10^(-5)

Ans: Rule: Negative exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the left by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is -5, so move the decimal point 5 places left, filling with zeros.
8.3 × 10^(-5) = 0.000083
Answer: 0.000083

Q: Q2(ii). Write in standard notation: 4.1 × 10^6

Ans: Rule: Positive exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the right by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is 6, so move the decimal point 6 places right, filling with zeros.
4.1 × 10^6 = 4100000
Answer: 4,100,000

Q: Q2(iii). Write in standard notation: 2.07 × 10^7

Ans: Rule: Positive exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the right by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is 7, so move the decimal point 7 places right, filling with zeros.
2.07 × 10^7 = 20700000
Answer: 20,700,000

Q: Q2(iv). Write in standard notation: 3.15 × 10^(-6)

Ans: Rule: Negative exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the left by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is -6, so move the decimal point 6 places left, filling with zeros.
3.15 × 10^(-6) = 0.00000315
Answer: 0.00000315

Q: Q2(v). Write in standard notation: 6.27 × 10^(-10)

Ans: Rule: Negative exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the left by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is -10, so move the decimal point 10 places left, filling with zeros.
6.27 × 10^(-10) = 0.000000000627
Answer: 0.000000000627

Q: Q2(vi). Write in standard notation: 5.41 × 10^(-8)

Ans: Rule: Negative exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the left by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is -8, so move the decimal point 8 places left, filling with zeros.
5.41 × 10^(-8) = 0.0000000541
Answer: 0.0000000541

Q: Q2(vii). Write in standard notation: 7.632 × 10^(-4)

Ans: Rule: Negative exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the left by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is -4, so move the decimal point 4 places left, filling with zeros.
7.632 × 10^(-4) = 0.0007632
Answer: 0.0007632

Q: Q2(viii). Write in standard notation: 9.4 × 10^5

Ans: Rule: Positive exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the right by the number of places equal to the exponent.
Exponent is 5, so move the decimal point 5 places right, filling with zeros.
9.4 × 10^5 = 940000
Answer: 940,000

Q: Q2(ix). Write in standard notation: -2.6 × 10^9

Ans: Rule: Positive exponent of 10 — move the decimal point to the right by the number of places equal to the exponent; the sign is carried along.
Exponent is 9, so move the decimal point 9 places right, filling with zeros.
-2.6 × 10^9 = -2600000000
Answer: -2,600,000,000

Q: Q3. How long does it take light to travel to Earth from the sun? The sun is 9.3 × 10^7 mi from Earth, and light travels 1.86 × 10^5 mi/s.

Ans: Rule: Time = Distance / Speed; use (a × 10^m)/(b × 10^n) = (a/b) × 10^(m - n) by the division law of indices.
Time = (9.3 × 10^7) / (1.86 × 10^5) seconds
= (9.3/1.86) × 10^(7 - 5) seconds
= 5 × 10² seconds
= 500 seconds
500 seconds = 480 seconds + 20 seconds = 8 minutes 20 seconds.
Answer: 500 seconds, i.e. 8 min and 20 sec.

mcqs.q: Write 405,000 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Scientific notation is a × 10^n with 1 ≤ a < 10. Move the decimal point 5 places left: 405000 → 4.05, so a = 4.05 and n = 5, giving 4.05 × 10^5.

mcqs.q: Write 0.00092 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: For 0 < x < 1, move the decimal point right and n is negative. Move it 4 places right: 0.00092 → 9.2, so a = 9.2 and n = -4, giving 9.2 × 10^(-4).

mcqs.q: Write 234,600,000,000 in scientific notation.
mcqs.why: Move the decimal point 11 places left: 234600000000 → 2.346, so a = 2.346 and n = 11, giving 2.346 × 10^11.

mcqs.q: Write 0.05 × 10^(-3) in scientific notation.
Write 8.3 × 10^(-5) in standard notation.
mcqs.why: The exponent is -5, so move the decimal point 5 places left, filling with zeros: 8.3 → 0.000083.

mcqs.q: Write 2.07 × 10^7 in standard notation.
mcqs.why: The exponent is 7, so move the decimal point 7 places right, filling with zeros: 2.07 → 20,700,000.

mcqs.q: Write 6.27 × 10^(-10) in standard notation.
mcqs.why: The exponent is -10, so move the decimal point 10 places left, filling with zeros: 6.27 → 0.000000000627.

mcqs.q: Write -2.6 × 10^9 in standard notation.
mcqs.why: The exponent is 9, so move the decimal point 9 places right, filling with zeros, and carry the negative sign along: -2.6 → -2,600,000,000.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is the correct scientific notation for 1,670,000?
mcqs.why: Scientific notation needs 1 ≤ a < 10, so a must be 1.67. Move the decimal point 6 places left: 1670000 → 1.67, so n = 6, giving 1.67 × 10^6. The other forms are equal in value but their coefficients break the rule 1 ≤ a < 10.

mcqs.q: The sun is 9.3 × 10^7 mi from Earth and light travels 1.86 × 10^5 mi/s. How long does light take to reach Earth?
mcqs.why: Time = Distance/Speed = (9.3 × 10^7)/(1.86 × 10^5) = (9.3/1.86) × 10^(7-5) = 5 × 10^2 = 500 seconds. Then 500 = 480 + 20 seconds = 8 minutes 20 seconds.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Definition of logarithm: a^x = y if and only if log_a y = x, where a > 0 and a ≠ 1.
  • log_a 1 = 0 for every valid base, because a^0 = 1; e.g. 10^0 = 1 gives log_10 1 = 0.
  • log_a a = 1, because a^1 = a.
  • To solve log_a y = x, rewrite in exponential form a^x = y and express both sides as powers of the same base, then compare exponents.
  • When the unknown is the number, x = a^(given value); e.g. log_2 x = 7 gives x = 2^7 = 128.
  • When the unknown is the base, solve the resulting power equation and keep the positive base; e.g. log_x 0.25 = 2 gives x^2 = 0.25, so x = 1/2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Write in logarithmic form: 4⁴ = 256

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x.
Here a = 4, x = 4, y = 256.
4⁴ = 256 ⇔ log_4 256 = 4
Answer: log_4 256 = 4

Q: Q1(ii). Write in logarithmic form: 2^(-6) = 1/64

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x.
Here a = 2, x = -6, y = 1/64.
2^(-6) = 1/64 ⇔ log_2 (1/64) = -6
Answer: log_2 (1/64) = -6

Q: Q1(iii). Write in logarithmic form: 10⁰ = 1

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x.
Here a = 10, x = 0, y = 1.
10⁰ = 1 ⇔ log_10 1 = 0
Answer: log_10 1 = 0

Q: Q1(iv). Write in logarithmic form: x^(3/4) = y

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x.
Here the base is x, the index is 3/4 and the number is y.
x^(3/4) = y ⇔ log_x y = 3/4
Answer: log_x y = 3/4

Q: Q1(v). Write in logarithmic form: 3^(-4) = 1/81

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x.
Here a = 3, x = -4, y = 1/81.
3^(-4) = 1/81 ⇔ log_3 (1/81) = -4
Answer: log_3 (1/81) = -4

Q: Q1(vi). Write in logarithmic form: 64^(2/3) = 16

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x.
Here a = 64, x = 2/3, y = 16.
64^(2/3) = 16 ⇔ log_64 16 = 2/3
Answer: log_64 16 = 2/3

Q: Q2(i). Write in exponential form: log_a (1/a²) = -2

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
Here the base is a, x = -2, y = 1/a².
log_a (1/a²) = -2 ⇔ a^(-2) = 1/a²
Answer: a^(-2) = 1/a²

Q: Q2(ii). Write in exponential form: log_2 (1/128) = -7

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
Here a = 2, x = -7, y = 1/128.
log_2 (1/128) = -7 ⇔ 2^(-7) = 1/128
Answer: 2^(-7) = 1/128

Q: Q2(iii). Write in exponential form: log_b 3 = 64

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
Here the base is b, x = 64, y = 3.
log_b 3 = 64 ⇔ b^64 = 3
Answer: b^64 = 3

Q: Q2(iv). Write in exponential form: log_a a = 1

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
Here the base is a, x = 1, y = a.
log_a a = 1 ⇔ a¹ = a
Answer: a¹ = a

Q: Q2(v). Write in exponential form: log_a 1 = 0

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
Here the base is a, x = 0, y = 1.
log_a 1 = 0 ⇔ a⁰ = 1
Answer: a⁰ = 1

Q: Q2(vi). Write in exponential form: log_4 (1/8) = -3/2

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
Here a = 4, x = -3/2, y = 1/8.
log_4 (1/8) = -3/2 ⇔ 4^(-3/2) = 1/8
Check: 4^(3/2) = (√4)³ = 8, so 4^(-3/2) = 1/8. ✓
Answer: 4^(-3/2) = 1/8

Q: Q3(i). Solve: log_√5 125 = x

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y; then express both sides as powers of the same base.
log_√5 125 = x ⇔ (√5)^x = 125
√5 = 5^(1/2), so (√5)^x = 5^(x/2).
125 = 5³.
5^(x/2) = 5³
Compare exponents: x/2 = 3.
x = 6
Answer: x = 6
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is x = 6. The printed key gives 4.

Q: Q3(ii). Solve: log_4 x = -3

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y (with the unknown in the appropriate place).
log_4 x = -3 ⇔ x = 4^(-3)
x = 1/(4³)
= 1/64
Answer: x = 1/64

Q: Q3(iii). Solve: log_81 9 = x

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y; then express both sides as powers of the same base.
log_81 9 = x ⇔ 81^x = 9
81 = 9², so (9²)^x = 9¹.
9^(2x) = 9¹
Compare exponents: 2x = 1.
x = 1/2
Answer: x = 1/2

Q: Q3(iv). Solve: log_3 (5x + 1) = 2

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
log_3 (5x + 1) = 2 ⇔ 5x + 1 = 3²
5x + 1 = 9
5x = 9 - 1 = 8
x = 8/5
Answer: x = 8/5

Q: Q3(v). Solve: log_2 x = 7

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
log_2 x = 7 ⇔ x = 2^7
2^7 = 128.
x = 128
Answer: x = 128

Q: Q3(vi). Solve: log_x 0.25 = 2

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y; the base of a logarithm is positive and ≠ 1.
log_x 0.25 = 2 ⇔ x² = 0.25
x² = (0.5)²
x = 0.5 (taking the positive base)
Answer: x = 1/2

Q: Q3(vii). Solve: log_x (0.001) = -3

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y; the base of a logarithm is positive and ≠ 1.
log_x (0.001) = -3 ⇔ x^(-3) = 0.001
x^(-3) = 1/1000 = 10^(-3)
So 1/x³ = 1/1000, giving x³ = 1000.
x = 10
Answer: x = 10

Q: Q3(viii). Solve: log_x (1/64) = -2

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y; the base of a logarithm is positive and ≠ 1.
log_x (1/64) = -2 ⇔ x^(-2) = 1/64
1/x² = 1/64
x² = 64 = 8²
x = 8 (taking the positive base)
Answer: x = 8

Q: Q3(ix). Solve: log_√3 x = 16

Ans: Rule (definition of logarithm): log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y.
log_√3 x = 16 ⇔ x = (√3)^16
(√3)^16 = 3^(16/2) = 3^8
3^8 = 6561.
x = 6561
Answer: x = 6561
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 6561. The printed key gives 6560.

mcqs.q: Write 4^4 = 256 in logarithmic form.
mcqs.why: By the definition a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x. Here a = 4, x = 4 and y = 256, so 4^4 = 256 ⇔ log_4 256 = 4.

mcqs.q: Write 2^(-6) = 1/64 in logarithmic form.
mcqs.why: By the definition a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x. Here a = 2, x = -6 and y = 1/64, so 2^(-6) = 1/64 ⇔ log_2 (1/64) = -6.

mcqs.q: Write 10^0 = 1 in logarithmic form.
mcqs.why: By the definition a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x. Here a = 10, x = 0 and y = 1, so 10^0 = 1 ⇔ log_10 1 = 0.

mcqs.q: Write 64^(2/3) = 16 in logarithmic form.
mcqs.why: By the definition a^x = y ⇔ log_a y = x. Here a = 64, x = 2/3 and y = 16, so 64^(2/3) = 16 ⇔ log_64 16 = 2/3.

mcqs.q: Write log_2 (1/128) = -7 in exponential form.
mcqs.why: By the definition log_a y = x ⇔ a^x = y. Here a = 2, x = -7 and y = 1/128, so log_2 (1/128) = -7 ⇔ 2^(-7) = 1/128.

mcqs.q: Write log_4 (1/8) = -3/2 in exponential form.
Solve: log_√5 125 = x
mcqs.why: log_√5 125 = x ⇔ (√5)^x = 125. Now √5 = 5^(1/2), so (√5)^x = 5^(x/2), and 125 = 5^3. Hence 5^(x/2) = 5^3, so x/2 = 3 and x = 6. Note: the book's printed key gives 4, which is wrong; the correct value is 6.

mcqs.q: Solve: log_4 x = -3
Solve: log_81 9 = x
mcqs.why: log_81 9 = x ⇔ 81^x = 9. Write 81 = 9^2, so (9^2)^x = 9^1, i.e. 9^(2x) = 9^1. Comparing exponents, 2x = 1, so x = 1/2.

mcqs.q: Solve: log_3 (5x + 1) = 2
Solve: log_2 x = 7
mcqs.why: log_2 x = 7 ⇔ x = 2^7. Computing the power: 2^7 = 128, so x = 128.

mcqs.q: Solve: log_x 0.25 = 2
mcqs.why: log_x 0.25 = 2 ⇔ x^2 = 0.25 = (0.5)^2. The base of a logarithm is positive and ≠ 1, so take the positive value x = 0.5 = 1/2.

mcqs.q: Solve: log_x (0.001) = -3
Solve: log_x (1/64) = -2
mcqs.why: log_x (1/64) = -2 ⇔ x^(-2) = 1/64. So 1/x^2 = 1/64, giving x^2 = 64 = 8^2. Taking the positive base, x = 8.

mcqs.q: Solve: log_√3 x = 16
mcqs.why: log_√3 x = 16 ⇔ x = (√3)^16 = 3^(16/2) = 3^8. Computing: 3^4 = 81 and 3^8 = 81^2 = 6561, so x = 6561. Note: the book's printed key gives 6560, which is wrong; the correct value is 6561.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • For a common logarithm, log x = characteristic + mantissa; the mantissa is always positive and depends only on the digits of x, while the characteristic depends on the position of the decimal point.
  • If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1; e.g. 7824 has 4 digits, so its characteristic is 3.
  • If 0 < x < 1, characteristic = -[(number of zeros immediately after the decimal point) + 1], written in bar notation; e.g. 0.71 has 0 such zeros, so its characteristic is -1.
  • Numbers with the same digits have the same mantissa: the mantissa for digits 872 is .9405, so log 87.2 = 1.9405.
  • For x < 1 the negative characteristic is written with a bar over it while the mantissa stays positive; e.g. log 0.00159 = 3̄.2014.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 57.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
57 has 2 digits before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 2 - 1 = 1.
Answer: 1

Q: Q1(ii). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 7.4.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
7.4 has 1 digit before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 1 - 1 = 0.
Answer: 0

Q: Q1(iii). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 5.63.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
5.63 has 1 digit before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 1 - 1 = 0.
Answer: 0

Q: Q1(iv). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 5.63.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
As printed, this number is the same as part (iii): 5.63 has 1 digit before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 1 - 1 = 0.
Answer: 0
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 0 for the number as printed (5.63). The printed key gives -1, which would be correct for 0.563.

Q: Q1(v). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 982.5.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
982.5 has 3 digits before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 3 - 1 = 2.
Answer: 2

Q: Q1(vi). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 7824.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
7824 has 4 digits before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 4 - 1 = 3.
Answer: 3

Q: Q1(vii). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 186000.

Ans: Rule: If x > 1, characteristic = (number of digits before the decimal point in x) - 1.
186000 has 6 digits before the decimal point.
Characteristic = 6 - 1 = 5.
Answer: 5

Q: Q1(viii). Find the characteristic of the common logarithm of 0.71.

Ans: Rule: If x < 1, characteristic = -[(number of zeros immediately after the decimal point) + 1].
0.71 has 0 zeros immediately after the decimal point (the first digit after the point, 7, is non-zero).
Characteristic = -(0 + 1) = -1.
Answer: -1
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is -1 for the number as printed (0.71). The printed key gives -3, which would be correct for 0.0071.

Q: Q2(i). Find log 87.2.

Ans: Rule: log x = characteristic + mantissa; the characteristic comes from the position of the decimal point and the mantissa from the log table (mantissa depends only on the digits of x).
87.2 has 2 digits before the decimal point, so characteristic = 2 - 1 = 1.
From the log table, mantissa for the digits 872 is .9405.
log 87.2 = 1 + .9405
Answer: 1.9405 (the book's key rounds this to 1.941)

Q: Q2(ii). Find log 37300.

Ans: Rule: log x = characteristic + mantissa; characteristic from the decimal position, mantissa from the log table.
37300 has 5 digits before the decimal point, so characteristic = 5 - 1 = 4.
From the log table, mantissa for the digits 373 is .5717.
log 37300 = 4 + .5717
Answer: 4.5717 (the book's key rounds this to 4.572)

Q: Q2(iii). Find log 753.

Ans: Rule: log x = characteristic + mantissa; characteristic from the decimal position, mantissa from the log table.
753 has 3 digits before the decimal point, so characteristic = 3 - 1 = 2.
From the log table, mantissa for the digits 753 is .8768.
log 753 = 2 + .8768
Answer: 2.8768 (the book's key rounds this to 2.877)

Q: Q2(iv). Find log 9.21.

Ans: Rule: log x = characteristic + mantissa; characteristic from the decimal position, mantissa from the log table.
9.21 has 1 digit before the decimal point, so characteristic = 1 - 1 = 0.
From the log table, mantissa for the digits 921 is .9643.
log 9.21 = 0 + .9643
Answer: 0.9643

Q: Q2(v). Find log 0.00159.

Ans: Rule: log x = characteristic + mantissa; for x < 1, characteristic = -[(zeros after the decimal point) + 1], written in bar notation, and the mantissa (always positive) comes from the log table.
0.00159 has 2 zeros immediately after the decimal point, so characteristic = -(2 + 1) = -3, written 3̄.
From the log table, mantissa for the digits 159 is .2014.
log 0.00159 = 3̄.2014
Answer: 3̄.2014

Q: Q2(vi). Find log 0.0256.

Ans: Rule: log x = characteristic + mantissa; for x < 1, characteristic = -[(zeros after the decimal point) + 1], written in bar notation, and the mantissa comes from the log table.

0.783 has 0 zeros immediately after the decimal point, so characteristic = -(0 + 1) = -1, written 1̄.

Q: Q3(vi). Find the logarithm of 0.09566.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • If log x = y then x = antilog y: the antilogarithm reverses the logarithm.
  • To find an antilog, the digits are read from the antilog table using the mantissa only.
  • For a positive characteristic c, the number has c + 1 digits before the decimal point; e.g. characteristic 2 gives 3 digits before the point.
  • For a negative characteristic -k (bar k), there are k - 1 zeros between the decimal point and the first significant digit.
  • The same mantissa gives the same digit sequence wherever the decimal point falls: mantissa .2508 gives the digits 1781 in both 17.81 and 0.01781.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the anti-logarithm of 1.2508.

Ans: Rule: If log x = y then x = antilog y; the digits come from the antilog table using the mantissa, and the characteristic fixes the decimal point (digits before the point = characteristic + 1).
Characteristic = 1, mantissa = .2508.
From the antilog table, mantissa .2508 gives the digits 1781.
Characteristic 1 means 1 + 1 = 2 digits before the decimal point.
So the number is 17.81.
Answer: 17.81

Q: Q1(ii). Find the anti-logarithm of 0.8401.

Ans: Rule: If log x = y then x = antilog y; digits from the antilog table using the mantissa, characteristic fixes the decimal point.
Characteristic = 0, mantissa = .8401.
From the antilog table, mantissa .8401 gives the digits 6920.
Characteristic 0 means 0 + 1 = 1 digit before the decimal point.
So the number is 6.920.
Answer: 6.920

Q: Q1(iii). Find the anti-logarithm of 2.540.

Ans: Rule: If log x = y then x = antilog y; digits from the antilog table using the mantissa, characteristic fixes the decimal point.
Write 2.540 as 2.5400: characteristic = 2, mantissa = .5400.
From the antilog table, mantissa .5400 gives the digits 3467.
Characteristic 2 means 2 + 1 = 3 digits before the decimal point.
So the number is 346.7.
Answer: 346.7

Q: Q1(iv). Find the anti-logarithm of 2̄.2508.

Ans: Rule: If log x = y then x = antilog y; for a negative characteristic -k, there are (k - 1) zeros between the decimal point and the first significant digit.
Characteristic = -2 (bar 2), mantissa = .2508.
From the antilog table, mantissa .2508 gives the digits 1781.
Characteristic -2 means 2 - 1 = 1 zero after the decimal point before the first digit.
So the number is 0.01781.
Answer: 0.01781

Q: Q1(v). Find the anti-logarithm of 1̄.5463.

Ans: Rule: If log x = y then x = antilog y; for a negative characteristic -k, there are (k - 1) zeros between the decimal point and the first significant digit.
Characteristic = -1 (bar 1), mantissa = .5463.
From the antilog table, mantissa .5463 gives the digits 3518.
Characteristic -1 means 1 - 1 = 0 zeros after the decimal point, so the first digit comes immediately after the point.
So the number is 0.3518.
Answer: 0.3518

Q: Q1(vi). Find the anti-logarithm of 3.5526.

Ans: Rule: If log x = y then x = antilog y; digits from the antilog table using the mantissa, characteristic fixes the decimal point.
Characteristic = 3, mantissa = .5526.
From the antilog table, mantissa .5526 gives the digits 3570.
Characteristic 3 means 3 + 1 = 4 digits before the decimal point.
So the number is 3570.
Answer: 3570.0

Q: Q2(i). Find the value of x: log x = 1̄.8401

Ans: Rule: log x = y means x = antilog y; digits from the antilog table using the mantissa, position from the characteristic.
x = antilog (1̄.8401)
Mantissa .8401 gives the digits 6920.
Characteristic -1 means the first digit comes immediately after the decimal point.
So x = 0.6920.
Answer: x = 0.6920

Q: Q2(ii). Find the value of x: log x = 2.1931

Ans: Rule: log x = y means x = antilog y.
x = antilog (2.1931)

So x = 156.0.
Answer: x = 156.0

Q: Q2(iii). Find the value of x: log x = 4.5911

x = antilog (4.5911)

Characteristic 4 means 5 digits before the decimal point.
So x = 39000.
Answer: x = 39000.0

Q: Q2(iv). Find the value of x: log x = 3̄.0253

x = antilog (3̄.0253)
Mantissa .0253 gives the digits 1060.
With 2 zeros after the decimal point, x = 0.001060.
Answer: x = 0.001060

Q: Q2(v). Find the value of x: log x = 1.8716

Ans: Rule: log x = y means x = antilog y.
x = antilog (1.8716)
Mantissa .8716 gives the digits 7440.
Characteristic 1 means 2 digits before the decimal point.
So x = 74.40.

x = antilog (2̄.8370)
