Ans: Method: Factorize by grouping and by the identities a² - x² = (a - x)(a + x), x² - 2ax + a² = (x - a)² = (a - x)², x² + (a + b)x + ab = (x + a)(x + b).
ax + ab + cx + bc = a(x + b) + c(x + b) = (x + b)(a + c).
= [(x + b)(a + c)(a - x)²]/[(a - x)(a + x)(x + a)(x + b)]
Cancel (x + b) and one (a - x): = (a + c)(a - x)/(x + a)²
Answer: (a + c)(a - x)/(x + a)²

mcqs.q: Simplify: x/(x + y) + 2y/(x + y)
mcqs.why: The denominators are already the same, so keep (x + y) and add the numerators: (x + 2y)/(x + y). No factor is common to the numerator and denominator, so nothing cancels. Simplified form: (x + 2y)/(x + y).
Take L.C.M. = (y - 2)(y + 2) = y^2 - 4. The numerator becomes 3(y + 2) - 2(y - 2) - y = 3y + 6 - 2y + 4 - y = 10. So the result is 10/(y^2 - 4).
Factorize x^2 - y^2 = (x + y)(x - y) and use it as L.C.M. Numerator: (x - y)(x - y) - (x^2 - 2y^2) = x^2 - 2xy + y^2 - x^2 + 2y^2 = 3y^2 - 2xy. Result: (3y^2 - 2xy)/(x^2 - y^2).

mcqs.q: Simplify: a/(3x - y) + a/(3x + y) - 6ax/(9x^2 - y^2)
mcqs.why: Use L.C.M. = 9x^2 - y^2 = (3x - y)(3x + y). Numerator: a(3x + y) + a(3x - y) - 6ax = 3ax + ay + 3ax - ay - 6ax = 0. So the whole expression is 0/(9x^2 - y^2) = 0.

Factorize x^3 + y^3 = (x + y)(x^2 - xy + y^2) and x^3 - y^3 = (x - y)(x^2 + xy + y^2) and cancel: the first two fractions become 1/(x + y) and 1/(x - y). With L.C.M. (x + y)(x - y), the numerator is (x - y) + (x + y) - 1 = 2x - 1. Result: (2x - 1)/(x^2 - y^2).

mcqs.q: Simplify: (x^2 - 25)/(5 - x)
mcqs.why: Factorize the numerator: x^2 - 25 = (x - 5)(x + 5). Note 5 - x = -(x - 5). So the fraction is (x - 5)(x + 5) / (-(x - 5)) = -(x + 5) after cancelling (x - 5).

Factorize: x^2 + 5x + 4 = (x + 1)(x + 4) and x^2 + 3x + 2 = (x + 1)(x + 2). The product is [(x + 1)(x + 4) x 2y^2] / [4y^3(x + 1)(x + 2)]. Cancel (x + 1) and 2y^2: the result is (x + 4)/(2y(x + 2)). Note: the book's printed answer for this question is incorrect; this cancelled form is correct.

mcqs.q: Simplify: a(a + b)/(a^3 - b^3) x (a^2 + ab + b^2)/(a^2 - b^2)
mcqs.why: Factorize a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) and a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b). The product is a(a + b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) / [(a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)(a - b)(a + b)]. Cancel (a + b) and (a^2 + ab + b^2): the result is a/(a - b)^2.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 7/(x^2 - 4) / (xy/(x + 2))
mcqs.why: Multiply by the reciprocal and factorize x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2): 7/((x - 2)(x + 2)) x (x + 2)/(xy). Cancel (x + 2): the result is 7/(xy(x - 2)).

Multiply by the reciprocal. Factorize a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) and a^4 - b^4 = (a - b)(a + b)(a^2 + b^2). The expression becomes [(a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2)(a^2 + b^2)] / [(a - b)(a + b)(a^2 + b^2)(a^2 + ab + b^2)]. Cancel (a - b), (a^2 + ab + b^2) and (a^2 + b^2): the result is 1/(a + b).

Multiply by the reciprocal. Factorize 3x - 12 = 3(x - 4), x^2 - 2x = x(x - 2), x^2 - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4). The expression is [2x/(3(x - 4))] x [(x - 2)(x - 4)/(x(x - 2))]. Cancel x, (x - 2) and (x - 4): the result is 2/3.

Factorize: a^4 - 8a = a(a - 2)(a^2 + 2a + 4) since a^3 - 8 = (a - 2)(a^2 + 2a + 4); 2a^2 + 5a - 3 = (2a - 1)(a + 3); a^2 - 2a = a(a - 2). Changing the division to multiplication by the reciprocal, the full product is [a(a - 2)(a^2 + 2a + 4)(2a - 1)(a + 3)] / [(2a - 1)(a + 3)(a^2 + 2a + 4) x a(a - 2)]. Every factor cancels, leaving 1.

Multiply by the reciprocal. Factorize 9 - x^2 = (3 - x)(3 + x), x^4 + 6x^3 = x^3(x + 6), x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x = x(x - 3)(x + 1), x^2 + 7x + 6 = (x + 1)(x + 6). After cancelling (x + 1) and (x + 6), the factor (3 - x)/(x - 3) = -1 remains, giving -(3 + x)/x^4 = -(x + 3)/x^4. Note: the book's printed answer misses this minus sign and is incorrect.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Square root by factorization: write the expression as a perfect square (a + b)^2 or (a - b)^2; the square root is then the bracket with a + or - sign, e.g. x^2 + 4x + 4 = (x + 2)^2 gives +-(x + 2).
  • A repeated block is treated as one quantity: with t = x + y, (x + y)^2 + 6(x + y) + 9 = (t + 3)^2.
  • Use x^2 + 1/x^2 = (x + 1/x)^2 - 2 and x^2 + 1/x^2 = (x - 1/x)^2 + 2 to reduce expressions in x and 1/x to a quadratic in one quantity.
  • The square root of a fraction is the square root of the numerator divided by the square root of the denominator.
  • Square root by division: the first term of the root is the square root of the first term; each next term is found by dividing the first term of the remainder by twice the root found so far.
  • To make an expression a perfect square, the final division remainder must be zero: add the negative of the remainder, or subtract the remainder itself.
  • Comparing coefficients of an assumed root works too: 4x^4 + 32x^2 + 96 + 128/x^2 + k/x^4 with root 2x^2 + 8 + 8/x^2 gives k = 64.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the square root by factorization method: x² + 4x + 4.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - write the expression as a perfect square (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², then take the square root.
x² + 4x + 4 = (x)² + 2(x)(2) + (2)² = (x + 2)²
√((x + 2)²) = ±(x + 2)
Answer: ±(x + 2)

Q: Q1(ii). Find the square root by factorization method: (x + y)² + 6(x + y) + 9.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - treat (x + y) as one quantity and complete the perfect square.
Let t = x + y. Then the expression is t² + 6t + 9 = t² + 2(t)(3) + 3² = (t + 3)².
Putting t back: = (x + y + 3)²
Square root = ±(x + y + 3)
Answer: ±(x + y + 3)

Q: Q1(iii). Find the square root by factorization method: x²y² - 8xy + 16.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - write as (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b² with a = xy, b = 4.
x²y² - 8xy + 16 = (xy)² - 2(xy)(4) + (4)² = (xy - 4)²
Square root = ±(xy - 4)
Answer: ±(xy - 4)

Q: Q1(iv). Find the square root by factorization method: x² + 1/x² - 8(x + 1/x) + 18.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - put t = x + 1/x and use x² + 1/x² = t² - 2.
x² + 1/x² - 8(x + 1/x) + 18 = (t² - 2) - 8t + 18 = t² - 8t + 16
= t² - 2(t)(4) + 4² = (t - 4)²
Putting t back: = (x + 1/x - 4)²
Answer: ±(x + 1/x - 4)

Q: Q1(v). Find the square root by factorization method: x(x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3) + 1.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - pair the factors so that both pairs give the same quadratic.
x(x + 3) = x² + 3x; (x + 1)(x + 2) = x² + 3x + 2.
Let u = x² + 3x. Expression = u(u + 2) + 1 = u² + 2u + 1 = (u + 1)².
Putting u back: = (x² + 3x + 1)²
Answer: ±(x² + 3x + 1)

Q: Q1(vi). Find the square root by factorization method: (x² + 1/x²)² - 5(x - 1/x) + 9/4.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - put t = x - 1/x and use x² + 1/x² = t² + 2.
Note on the printed question: as printed, with (x² + 1/x²)² and constant 9/4, the expression is not a perfect square. The book's own printed answer fits the expression x² + 1/x² - 5(x - 1/x) + 17/4, which is solved here.
x² + 1/x² - 5(x - 1/x) + 17/4 = (t² + 2) - 5t + 17/4 = t² - 5t + 25/4
= t² - 2(t)(5/2) + (5/2)² = (t - 5/2)²
Putting t back: = (x - 1/x - 5/2)²
Answer: ±(x - 1/x - 5/2)
Note: The question as printed in the book contains misprints (an extra square on the first term and 9/4 for 17/4); with those corrections the answer above agrees with the book's printed answer.

Q: Q1(vii). Find the square root by factorization method: (x² + 1/x²)² - 4(x + 1/x)² + 12.

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - put s = x² + 1/x² and use (x + 1/x)² = s + 2.
Expression = s² - 4(s + 2) + 12 = s² - 4s - 8 + 12 = s² - 4s + 4
= (s - 2)²
Putting s back: = (x² + 1/x² - 2)²
Answer: ±(x² + 1/x² - 2)

Q: Q1(viii). Find the square root by factorization method: (4x⁶ - 12x³y³ + 9y⁶)/(9x⁴ + 24x²y² + 16y⁴).

Ans: Method: Square root by factorization - the square root of a fraction is the square root of the numerator divided by the square root of the denominator; write each as a perfect square.
Numerator: 4x⁶ - 12x³y³ + 9y⁶ = (2x³)² - 2(2x³)(3y³) + (3y³)² = (2x³ - 3y³)²
Denominator: 9x⁴ + 24x²y² + 16y⁴ = (3x²)² + 2(3x²)(4y²) + (4y²)² = (3x² + 4y²)²
Square root = ±(2x³ - 3y³)/(3x² + 4y²)
Answer: ±(2x³ - 3y³)/(3x² + 4y²)

Q: Q2(i). Find the square root by division method: 4x⁴ - 4x³ + 13x² - 6x + 9.

Ans: Method: Square root by division - write in descending order; first term of the root is the square root of the first term; each next term is found by dividing the first term of the remainder by twice the part of the root already found, then subtracting.
√(4x⁴) = 2x². Subtract (2x²)² = 4x⁴: remainder -4x³ + 13x² - 6x + 9.
Second term: -4x³/(2 × 2x²) = -x. Subtract (-x)(4x² - x) = -4x³ + x²: remainder 12x² - 6x + 9.
Third term: 12x²/(4x²) = 3. Subtract 3(4x² - 2x + 3) = 12x² - 6x + 9: remainder 0.
Root = 2x² - x + 3. Check: (2x² - x + 3)² = 4x⁴ - 4x³ + 13x² - 6x + 9. ✓
Answer: ±(2x² - x + 3)

Q: Q2(ii). Find the square root by division method: x⁴ + x³ - (31/4)x² - 4x + 16.

Ans: Method: Square root by division - same steps as the book's rules: descending order, divide the first term of each remainder by twice the root found so far, multiply and subtract.
√(x⁴) = x². Subtract x⁴: remainder x³ - (31/4)x² - 4x + 16.
Second term: x³/(2x²) = x/2. Subtract (x/2)(2x² + x/2) = x³ + x²/4: remainder -8x² - 4x + 16.
Third term: -8x²/(2x²) = -4. Subtract (-4)(2x² + x - 4) = -8x² - 4x + 16: remainder 0.
Root = x² + x/2 - 4. Check: (x² + x/2 - 4)² = x⁴ + x³ - (31/4)x² - 4x + 16. ✓
Answer: ±(x² + x/2 - 4)

Q: Q2(iii). Find the square root by division method: x² - 2x + 1 + 2xy - 2y + y².

Ans: Method: Square root by division - arrange the terms as a perfect square in x and y and apply the division steps (equivalently, recognize the square and verify it).
Try root x + y - 1: (x + y - 1)² = x² + y² + 1 + 2xy - 2x - 2y.
This is exactly x² - 2x + 1 + 2xy - 2y + y², so the division ends with remainder 0 at this root.
Answer: ±(x + y - 1)

Q: Q2(iv). Find the square root by division method: (x² - 1/x²)² - 12(x² - 1/x²) + 36.

Ans: Method: Put t = x² - 1/x²; the expression is a quadratic in t, and the division method on it gives a two-term root.
Expression = t² - 12t + 36.
√(t²) = t. Subtract t²: remainder -12t + 36.
Second term: -12t/(2t) = -6. Subtract (-6)(2t - 6) = -12t + 36: remainder 0.
Root = t - 6 = x² - 1/x² - 6.
Answer: ±(x² - 1/x² - 6)

Q: Q3. For what value of k will the expression 4x⁴ + 32x² + 96 + 128/x² + k/x⁴ become a perfect square?

Ans: Method: Assume the square root has the form 2x² + p + q/x² and compare coefficients after squaring (the division method gives the same result).
(2x² + p + q/x²)² = 4x⁴ + p² + q²/x⁴ + 4p x² + 4q + 2pq/x².
Compare x² terms: 4p = 32, so p = 8.
Compare constant terms: p² + 4q = 96, so 64 + 4q = 96, giving q = 8.
Check 1/x² terms: 2pq = 2 × 8 × 8 = 128. ✓ matches the given expression.
Then k = q² = 8² = 64.
Answer: k = 64

Q: Q4(i). What should be added to the expression 4x⁴ - 12x³ + 17x² - 13x + 6 so that it becomes a perfect square?

Ans: Method: Find the square root by the division method; the expression is a perfect square exactly when the final remainder is made zero, so the quantity to add is the negative of the remainder.
Division gives root 2x² - 3x + 2 with remainder -x + 2, because (2x² - 3x + 2)² = 4x⁴ - 12x³ + 17x² - 12x + 4 and the given expression exceeds this by -x + 2.
To cancel the remainder, add -(-x + 2) = x - 2.
Answer: x - 2 should be added

Q: Q4(ii). What should be subtracted from the expression 4x⁴ - 12x³ + 17x² - 13x + 6 so that it becomes a perfect square?

Ans: Method: Same division as in part (i): root 2x² - 3x + 2, remainder -x + 2.
Subtracting the remainder itself makes the remainder zero.
Check: (4x⁴ - 12x³ + 17x² - 13x + 6) - (-x + 2) = 4x⁴ - 12x³ + 17x² - 12x + 4 = (2x² - 3x + 2)². ✓
Answer: -x + 2 should be subtracted

Q: Q4(iii). For what value of x will the expression 4x⁴ - 12x³ + 17x² - 13x + 6 become a perfect square?

Ans: Method: From parts (i) and (ii), the division remainder is -x + 2; the expression is a perfect square exactly when this remainder is zero.
-x + 2 = 0
x = 2
Check: at x = 2 the expression equals (2(2)² - 3(2) + 2)² = (8 - 6 + 2)² = 16, and directly 4(16) - 12(8) + 17(4) - 13(2) + 6 = 64 - 96 + 68 - 26 + 6 = 16. ✓
Answer: x = 2

Q: Q5. What should be subtracted and added to the expression x⁴ - 4x³ + 10x + 7 so that the expression is made a perfect square?

Ans: Method: Find the square root by the division method (write the missing x² term as 0x²); the final remainder tells what to subtract, and its negative tells what to add.
√(x⁴) = x². Subtract x⁴: remainder -4x³ + 0x² + 10x + 7.
Second term: -4x³/(2x²) = -2x. Subtract (-2x)(2x² - 2x) = -4x³ + 4x²: remainder -4x² + 10x + 7.
Third term: -4x²/(2x²) = -2. Subtract (-2)(2x² - 4x - 2) = -4x² + 8x + 4: remainder 2x + 3.
So (x² - 2x - 2)² = x⁴ - 4x³ + 10x + 4, and the given expression is 2x + 3 more than this square.
Subtract 2x + 3, or equivalently add -(2x + 3) = -2x - 3.
Answer: Subtract 2x + 3; add -2x - 3

Q: Q6(i). Find the values of l and m for which the expression x⁴ + 4x³ + 16x² + lx + m will become a perfect square.

Ans: Method: Assume the square root is x² + 2x + c (the second term is fixed by 2 × x² × (second term) = 4x³) and compare coefficients.
(x² + 2x + c)² = x⁴ + 4x³ + (2c + 4)x² + 4cx + c², expanding term by term: (x²)² = x⁴; 2(x²)(2x) = 4x³; 2(x²)(c) + (2x)² = (2c + 4)x²; 2(2x)(c) = 4cx; c².
Compare x² terms: 2c + 4 = 16, so c = 6.
Then l = 4c = 24 and m = c² = 36.
Check: (x² + 2x + 6)² = x⁴ + 4x³ + 16x² + 24x + 36. ✓
Answer: l = 24, m = 36

Q: Q6(ii). Find the values of l and m for which the expression 49x⁴ - 70x³ + 109x² + lx - m will become a perfect square.

Ans: Method: Assume the square root is 7x² - 5x + c (the x-term is fixed by 2 × 7x² × (second term) = -70x³) and compare coefficients.
(7x² - 5x + c)² = 49x⁴ - 70x³ + (25 + 14c)x² - 10c x + c², expanding term by term.
Compare x² terms: 25 + 14c = 109, so 14c = 84 and c = 6.
Then l = -10c = -60, and the constant term is c² = 36 = -m, so m = -36.
Check: (7x² - 5x + 6)² = 49x⁴ - 70x³ + 109x² - 60x + 36. ✓
Answer: l = -60, m = -36

mcqs.q: Find the square root by factorization of x^2 + 4x + 4
mcqs.why: Write as a perfect square: x^2 + 4x + 4 = (x)^2 + 2(x)(2) + (2)^2 = (x + 2)^2. Taking the square root gives +-(x + 2), since both (x + 2)^2 and (-(x + 2))^2 equal the expression.

mcqs.q: Find the square root by factorization of (x + y)^2 + 6(x + y) + 9
mcqs.why: Put t = x + y: the expression is t^2 + 6t + 9 = t^2 + 2(t)(3) + 3^2 = (t + 3)^2. Putting t back gives (x + y + 3)^2, whose square root is +-(x + y + 3).

mcqs.q: Find the square root by factorization of x^2y^2 - 8xy + 16
mcqs.why: Write as (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2 with a = xy, b = 4: (xy)^2 - 2(xy)(4) + 4^2 = x^2y^2 - 8xy + 16, so the expression is (xy - 4)^2. Its square root is +-(xy - 4).

mcqs.q: Find the square root by factorization of x(x + 1)(x + 2)(x + 3) + 1
mcqs.why: Pair the factors: x(x + 3) = x^2 + 3x and (x + 1)(x + 2) = x^2 + 3x + 2. Put u = x^2 + 3x: the expression is u(u + 2) + 1 = u^2 + 2u + 1 = (u + 1)^2 = (x^2 + 3x + 1)^2. Square root: +-(x^2 + 3x + 1).

mcqs.q: Find the square root by factorization of (4x^6 - 12x^3y^3 + 9y^6)/(9x^4 + 24x^2y^2 + 16y^4)
Find the square root by the division method of 4x^4 - 4x^3 + 13x^2 - 6x + 9
mcqs.why: Division steps: sqrt(4x^4) = 2x^2; next term -4x^3/(2 x 2x^2) = -x; next term 12x^2/(4x^2) = 3, ending with remainder 0. Root = 2x^2 - x + 3. Check: (2x^2 - x + 3)^2 = 4x^4 - 4x^3 + (1 + 12)x^2 - 6x + 9 = 4x^4 - 4x^3 + 13x^2 - 6x + 9. So the square root is +-(2x^2 - x + 3).

mcqs.q: Find the square root by the division method of x^4 + x^3 - (31/4)x^2 - 4x + 16
mcqs.why: Division steps: sqrt(x^4) = x^2; next term x^3/(2x^2) = x/2; after subtracting, the remainder starts with -8x^2, giving next term -8x^2/(2x^2) = -4, and the remainder becomes 0. Root = x^2 + x/2 - 4. Check: (x^2 + x/2 - 4)^2 = x^4 + x^3 + (1/4 - 8)x^2 - 4x + 16 = x^4 + x^3 - (31/4)x^2 - 4x + 16.

mcqs.q: For what value of k does 4x^4 + 32x^2 + 96 + 128/x^2 + k/x^4 become a perfect square?
mcqs.why: Assume the root is 2x^2 + p + q/x^2. Squaring gives 4x^4 + 4p x^2 + (p^2 + 4q) + 2pq/x^2 + q^2/x^4. Compare: 4p = 32 gives p = 8; p^2 + 4q = 96 gives 64 + 4q = 96, so q = 8. Check: 2pq = 128, matching. Then k = q^2 = 8^2 = 64.

mcqs.q: What should be added to 4x^4 - 12x^3 + 17x^2 - 13x + 6 so that it becomes a perfect square?
mcqs.why: By division the root is 2x^2 - 3x + 2 with remainder -x + 2, because (2x^2 - 3x + 2)^2 = 4x^4 - 12x^3 + 17x^2 - 12x + 4 and the given expression exceeds this square by -x + 2. To cancel the remainder, add its negative: -(-x + 2) = x - 2.

mcqs.q: Find l and m for which x^4 + 4x^3 + 16x^2 + lx + m is a perfect square
mcqs.why: Assume the root is x^2 + 2x + c (the 2x is fixed by 2(x^2)(2x) = 4x^3). Squaring: x^4 + 4x^3 + (2c + 4)x^2 + 4cx + c^2. Compare x^2 terms: 2c + 4 = 16, so c = 6. Then l = 4c = 24 and m = c^2 = 36. Check: (x^2 + 2x + 6)^2 = x^4 + 4x^3 + 16x^2 + 24x + 36.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The H.C.F. of a^3 - 8b^3 = (a - 2b)(a^2 + 2ab + 4b^2) and a^2 - 4ab + 4b^2 = (a - 2b)^2 is (a - 2b).
  • For powers of the same expression, the L.C.M. takes the highest power and the H.C.F. takes the lowest power.
  • The H.C.F. of a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2) and a^2 + ab + b^2 is (a^2 + ab + b^2) itself, since the second expression is a factor of the first.
  • To reduce a fraction to lowest terms, factorize numerator and denominator and cancel the common factors.
  • L.C.M. = (A x B)/H.C.F. for any two expressions A and B.
  • Since a^3 + 1 = (a + 1)(a^2 - a + 1), the L.C.M. of a^2 - a + 1 and a^3 + 1 is a^3 + 1.
  • The square root of x^4 + 4x^3 + 6x^2 + 4x + 1 is +-(x^2 + 2x + 1), because the expression is ((x + 1)^2)^2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). H.C.F of a³ - 8b³ and a² - 4ab + 4b² is

Options: (a) a - 2b (b) a² + 2ab + b² (c) a + 2b (d) (a + 2b)²

Correct answer: a - 2b

Q: Q1(ii). L.C.M of (2x + 3y)⁵ and (2x + 3y)³ is

Options: (a) 2x + 3y (b) (2x + 3y)³ (c) (2x + 3y)² (d) (2x + 3y)⁵

Correct answer: (2x + 3y)⁵

Q: Q1(iii). H.C.F of a³ - b³ and a² + ab + b² is

Options: (a) a + b (b) a² + ab + b² (c) a - b (d) (a - b)²

Correct answer: a² + ab + b²

Q: Q1(iv). L.C.M of (a - b)⁴ and (a - b)³ is

Options: (a) (a - b) (b) (a - b)³ (c) (a - b)⁴ (d) (a - b)⁷

Correct answer: (a - b)⁴

Q: Q1(v). Reduce to lowest terms: 10(x + 3)(x - 2)/(15(x - 2))

Options: (a) 2(x + 3)/3 (b) 2x (c) 10(x + 3)/15 (d) 2(x + 1)

Correct answer: 2(x + 3)/3

Q: Q1(vi). Simplified form of b/(25a² - b²) - 1/(5a - b) is

Options: (a) 5a/(25a² - b²) (b) 5a/(5a - b) (c) -5a/(5a + b) (d) -5a/(25a² - b²)

Correct answer: -5a/(25a² - b²)

Q: Q1(vii). 5/(x² - x - 2) + 3/(x² + 4x + 3) =

Options: (a) (8x + 21)/((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3)) (b) (8x - 3)/((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3)) (c) (8x + 6)/((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3)) (d) (8x + 9)/((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3))

Correct answer: (8x + 9)/((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3))

Q: Q1(viii). (x² - 2x - 3)/(3x² + x - 2) in lowest terms is

Options: (a) (x - 3)/(3x - 2) (b) (-2x - 3)/(3x - 2) (c) (-2x - 2)/(x + 1) (d) (x - 3)/(3x + 2)

Correct answer: (x - 3)/(3x - 2)

Q: Q1(ix). L.C.M =

Options: (a) H.C.F/(A × B) (b) (A × B)/H.C.F (c) A/H.C.F (d) B/H.C.F

Correct answer: (A × B)/H.C.F

Q: Q1(x). L.C.M of a² - a + 1 and a³ + 1 is

Options: (a) a + 1 (b) a² - a + 1 (c) a³ + 1 (d) a² + a + 1

Correct answer: a³ + 1

Q: Q2(i). Simplify: 5/(2s + 4) - 3/(s² + 3s + 2) + s/(s² - s - 2).

Ans: Method: Factorize: 2s + 4 = 2(s + 2), s² + 3s + 2 = (s + 1)(s + 2), s² - s - 2 = (s - 2)(s + 1). L.C.M = 2(s + 2)(s + 1)(s - 2).
Numerator: 5(s + 1)(s - 2) - 3 × 2(s - 2) + s × 2(s + 2)
= 5(s² - s - 2) - 6s + 12 + 2s² + 4s = 5s² - 5s - 10 - 6s + 12 + 2s² + 4s
= 7s² - 7s + 2.
Answer: (7s² - 7s + 2)/(2(s + 2)(s + 1)(s - 2))

Q: Q2(ii). Simplify: a/((c - a)(a - b)) + b/((a - b)(b - c)) + c/((b - c)(c - a)).

Ans: Method: Take L.C.M = (a - b)(b - c)(c - a) and rewrite each term over it.
First term = a(b - c)/((a - b)(b - c)(c - a)); second = b(c - a)/((a - b)(b - c)(c - a)); third = c(a - b)/((a - b)(b - c)(c - a)).
Numerator: a(b - c) + b(c - a) + c(a - b) = ab - ac + bc - ab + ac - bc = 0.
Answer: 0

Q: Q2(iii). Simplify: (x² - 4)/(xy²) × 2xy/(x² - 4x + 4).

Ans: Method: Factorize x² - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2) and x² - 4x + 4 = (x - 2)², then cancel.
= [(x - 2)(x + 2) × 2xy]/[xy² × (x - 2)²]
Cancel (x - 2) and xy: = 2(x + 2)/(y(x - 2))
Answer: 2(x + 2)/(y(x - 2))

Q: Q2(iv). Simplify: (a³ - b³)/(a⁴ - b⁴) ÷ (a² + ab + b²)/(a² + b²).

Ans: Method: Multiply by the reciprocal and factorize a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²), a⁴ - b⁴ = (a - b)(a + b)(a² + b²).
= [(a - b)(a² + ab + b²)/((a - b)(a + b)(a² + b²))] × [(a² + b²)/(a² + ab + b²)]
Cancel (a - b), (a² + ab + b²) and (a² + b²): = 1/(a + b)
Answer: 1/(a + b)

Q: Q3. Find L.C.M of x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6 and x³ - 4x + 3.

Ans: Method: Use L.C.M by formula: first find the H.C.F by division, then L.C.M = (Product of the two polynomials)/H.C.F.
Division steps (as in the book's Example 7) give H.C.F = x - 1: indeed x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6 = (x - 1)(x² - 5x + 6) and x - 1 also divides x³ - 4x + 3.
L.C.M = [(x³ - 4x + 3)(x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6)]/(x - 1)
Divide x³ - 6x² + 11x - 6 by (x - 1): quotient x² - 5x + 6.
Answer: L.C.M = (x³ - 4x + 3)(x² - 5x + 6)

Q: Q4(i). Find the square root of: 4x² - 12x + 9.

Ans: Method: Write as a perfect square: 4x² - 12x + 9 = (2x)² - 2(2x)(3) + 3² = (2x - 3)².
Square root = ±(2x - 3).
Answer: ±(2x - 3)

Q: Q4(ii). Find the square root of: x⁴ + 4x³ + 6x² + 4x + 1.

Ans: Method: Recognize the binomial expansion (x + 1)⁴ = x⁴ + 4x³ + 6x² + 4x + 1, i.e. the expression is ((x + 1)²)².
(x + 1)² = x² + 2x + 1, and (x² + 2x + 1)² = x⁴ + 4x³ + 6x² + 4x + 1. ✓
Square root = ±(x² + 2x + 1).
Answer: ±(x² + 2x + 1)

Q: Q5. Simplify: (x³ - y³)/(x³ + z³) × (x² + xy + xz + yz)/(x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴) × (x³ + y³)/(x² - y²).

Ans: Method: Factorize: x³ - y³ = (x - y)(x² + xy + y²); x³ + z³ = (x + z)(x² - xz + z²); x² + xy + xz + yz = (x + y)(x + z); x⁴ + x²y² + y⁴ = (x² + xy + y²)(x² - xy + y²); x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² - xy + y²); x² - y² = (x - y)(x + y).
Product = [(x - y)(x² + xy + y²)(x + y)(x + z)(x + y)(x² - xy + y²)]/[(x + z)(x² - xz + z²)(x² + xy + y²)(x² - xy + y²)(x - y)(x + y)]
Cancel (x - y), (x + z), (x² + xy + y²), (x² - xy + y²) and one (x + y): = (x + y)/(x² - xz + z²)
Answer: (x + y)/(x² - xz + z²)

mcqs.q: The H.C.F. of a^3 - 8b^3 and a^2 - 4ab + 4b^2 is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Factorize: a^3 - 8b^3 = a^3 - (2b)^3 = (a - 2b)(a^2 + 2ab + 4b^2), and a^2 - 4ab + 4b^2 = (a - 2b)^2. The factor common to both, to the lowest power, is (a - 2b). So H.C.F. = a - 2b.

mcqs.q: The L.C.M. of (2x + 3y)^5 and (2x + 3y)^3 is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. For the L.C.M. of powers of the same expression, take the HIGHEST power: between (2x + 3y)^5 and (2x + 3y)^3 the highest is (2x + 3y)^5, which is a multiple of both. So L.C.M. = (2x + 3y)^5.

mcqs.q: The H.C.F. of a^3 - b^3 and a^2 + ab + b^2 is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Factorize a^3 - b^3 = (a - b)(a^2 + ab + b^2). The second expression, a^2 + ab + b^2, is itself one of these factors, so it divides a^3 - b^3 exactly. Hence H.C.F. = a^2 + ab + b^2.

mcqs.q: The L.C.M. of (a - b)^4 and (a - b)^3 is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. For the L.C.M. of powers of the same expression, take the HIGHEST power: between (a - b)^4 and (a - b)^3 the highest is (a - b)^4, which is a multiple of both. Powers are never added for an L.C.M.

mcqs.q: Reduce to lowest terms: 10(x + 3)(x - 2)/(15(x - 2))
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Cancel the common factor (x - 2) from numerator and denominator, and reduce 10/15 to 2/3: the result is 2(x + 3)/3. Check: 10(x + 3)(x - 2)/(15(x - 2)) = (10/15)(x + 3) = 2(x + 3)/3.

mcqs.q: The simplified form of b/(25a^2 - b^2) - 1/(5a - b) is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Factorize 25a^2 - b^2 = (5a - b)(5a + b) and use it as L.C.M.: 1/(5a - b) = (5a + b)/(25a^2 - b^2). Numerator: b - (5a + b) = -5a. Result: -5a/(25a^2 - b^2).

Book MCQ reused. Factorize: x^2 - x - 2 = (x - 2)(x + 1) and x^2 + 4x + 3 = (x + 1)(x + 3), so L.C.M. = (x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3). Numerator: 5(x + 3) + 3(x - 2) = 5x + 15 + 3x - 6 = 8x + 9. Result: (8x + 9)/((x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 3)).

mcqs.q: (x^2 - 2x - 3)/(3x^2 + x - 2) in lowest terms is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Factorize: x^2 - 2x - 3 = (x - 3)(x + 1) and 3x^2 + x - 2 = (3x - 2)(x + 1), since 3x^2 + 3x - 2x - 2 = 3x(x + 1) - 2(x + 1). Cancel (x + 1): the result is (x - 3)/(3x - 2).

mcqs.q: For two expressions A and B, L.C.M. equals
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. The rule for two expressions is A x B = H.C.F. x L.C.M. Dividing both sides by H.C.F. gives L.C.M. = (A x B)/H.C.F. This is the formula used throughout this unit.

mcqs.q: The L.C.M. of a^2 - a + 1 and a^3 + 1 is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Factorize a^3 + 1 = (a + 1)(a^2 - a + 1) by the sum of cubes. The first expression, a^2 - a + 1, is already a factor of a^3 + 1, so the L.C.M. is the larger expression itself: a^3 + 1.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A linear equation is solved by transferring terms: x-terms to one side and constants to the other, then dividing both sides by the coefficient of x.
  • 5x + 8 = 23 gives 5x = 15, so x = 3; always verify by substituting back into the original equation.
  • Equations with fractions are solved the same way: (3/5)x - 2/3 = 2 gives (3/5)x = 8/3 and x = 40/9.
  • Rational equations such as 2/(x - 1) = 1/(x - 2) are solved by cross-multiplication, valid for x not equal to 1 or 2, giving x = 3.
  • Brackets are removed first with the distributive property: 10(x - 4) = 4(2x - 1) + 5 becomes 10x - 40 = 8x + 1, so x = 41/2.
  • Word problems are turned into one linear equation: a number plus 3, doubled, equals 40 gives 2(x + 3) = 40 and x = 17.
  • Three consecutive odd integers are written x, x + 2, x + 4; their sum 81 gives x = 25, so the numbers are 25, 27, 29.
  • For a rectangle, perimeter = 2(length + breadth); breadth one fourth of length with perimeter 20 m gives length 8 m and breadth 2 m.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the solution set and verify: 5x + 8 = 23.

Ans: Method: Transfer the constant term to the other side, simplify, then divide both sides by the coefficient of x.
5x + 8 = 23
5x = 23 - 8 = 15
x = 15/5 = 3
Verify: L.H.S = 5(3) + 8 = 23 = R.H.S. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {3}

Q: Q1(ii). Find the solution set and verify: (3/5)x - 2/3 = 2.

Ans: Method: Transfer the constant term to the other side, simplify, then divide both sides by the coefficient of x.
(3/5)x = 2 + 2/3 = 8/3
x = (8/3) ÷ (3/5) = (8/3)(5/3) = 40/9
Verify: (3/5)(40/9) - 2/3 = 8/3 - 2/3 = 2 = R.H.S. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {40/9}

Q: Q1(iii). Find the solution set and verify: 6x - 5 = 2x + 9.

Ans: Method: Transfer all x-terms to one side and constants to the other, simplify, then divide by the coefficient of x.
6x - 2x = 9 + 5
4x = 14
x = 14/4 = 7/2
Verify: L.H.S = 6(7/2) - 5 = 21 - 5 = 16; R.H.S = 2(7/2) + 9 = 7 + 9 = 16. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {7/2}

Q: Q1(iv). Find the solution set and verify: 2/(x - 1) = 1/(x - 2).

Ans: Method: Cross-multiply (valid for x ≠ 1, 2), then solve the resulting linear equation.
2(x - 2) = 1(x - 1)
2x - 4 = x - 1
2x - x = -1 + 4
x = 3
Verify: L.H.S = 2/(3 - 1) = 1; R.H.S = 1/(3 - 2) = 1. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {3}

Q: Q1(v). Find the solution set and verify: 1/(7x + 13) = 2/9.

Ans: Method: Cross-multiply, then solve the resulting linear equation.
9 × 1 = 2(7x + 13)
9 = 14x + 26
14x = 9 - 26 = -17
x = -17/14
Verify: 7(-17/14) + 13 = -17/2 + 13 = 9/2, and 1/(9/2) = 2/9 = R.H.S. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {-17/14}

Q: Q1(vi). Find the solution set and verify: 10(x - 4) = 4(2x - 1) + 5.

Ans: Method: Remove the brackets using the distributive property, transfer x-terms to one side and constants to the other, then divide by the coefficient of x.
10x - 40 = 8x - 4 + 5
10x - 40 = 8x + 1
10x - 8x = 1 + 40
2x = 41
x = 41/2 = 20(1/2)
Verify: L.H.S = 10(41/2 - 4) = 10(33/2) = 165; R.H.S = 4(41 - 1) + 5 = 160 + 5 = 165. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {41/2}

Q: Q2. Awais thought of a number, added 3 with it. Then he doubled the sum, he got 40. What was the original number?

Ans: Method: Let the number be x, form a linear equation, and solve it.
Let the original number = x.
Adding 3 gives x + 3; doubling gives 2(x + 3) = 40.
2(x + 3) = 40
x + 3 = 20
x = 17
Verify: 17 + 3 = 20, doubled = 40. ✓
Answer: The original number was 17

Q: Q3. The sum of two numbers is -4 and their difference is 6. What are the numbers?

Ans: Method: Let the larger number be x; the other is x - 6 (difference 6). Use the sum to form one linear equation.
x + (x - 6) = -4
2x - 6 = -4
2x = 2
x = 1
Other number = 1 - 6 = -5.
Verify: 1 + (-5) = -4 and 1 - (-5) = 6. ✓
Answer: The numbers are 1 and -5

Q: Q4. The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 81. Find the numbers.

Ans: Method: Let the three consecutive odd integers be x, x + 2, x + 4 and use their sum.
x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 81
3x + 6 = 81
3x = 75
x = 25
The numbers are 25, 27, 29. Verify: 25 + 27 + 29 = 81. ✓
Answer: The numbers are 25, 27 and 29

Q: Q5. A man is 41 years old and his son is 9 years old. In how many years will the father be three times as old as the son?

Ans: Method: Let the required time be t years; after t years their ages are 41 + t and 9 + t.
41 + t = 3(9 + t)
41 + t = 27 + 3t
41 - 27 = 3t - t
14 = 2t
t = 7
Verify: after 7 years, father = 48, son = 16, and 48 = 3 × 16. ✓
Answer: In 7 years

Q: Q6. The tens digit of a certain two-digit number exceeds the units digit by 4 and is 1 less than twice the ones digit. Find the two-digit number.

Ans: Method: Let the units (ones) digit be x; then the tens digit is x + 4, and also 2x - 1.
x + 4 = 2x - 1
4 + 1 = 2x - x
x = 5
Tens digit = 5 + 4 = 9 (check: 2 × 5 - 1 = 9 ✓).
The number = 10 × 9 + 5 = 95.
Answer: The two-digit number is 95

Q: Q7. The sum of two digits is 10. If the places of the digits are changed then the new number is decreased by 18. Find the number.

Ans: Method: Let the tens digit be t and the units digit be u. Then t + u = 10, the number is 10t + u and the interchanged number is 10u + t.
(10t + u) - (10u + t) = 18
9t - 9u = 18, so t - u = 2.
Adding with t + u = 10: 2t = 12, so t = 6 and u = 4.
The number = 10 × 6 + 4 = 64. Verify: interchanged number 46, and 64 - 46 = 18. ✓
Answer: The number is 64
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 64 (46 is the interchanged number, not the original number).

Q: Q8. If breadth of a room is one fourth of its length and the perimeter of the room is 20 m, find length and breadth of the room.

Ans: Method: Let the length be l metres; then breadth = l/4. Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(length + breadth).
2(l + l/4) = 20
l + l/4 = 10
(5/4)l = 10
l = 8
Breadth = 8/4 = 2. Verify: perimeter = 2(8 + 2) = 20 m. ✓
Answer: Length = 8 m, breadth = 2 m

mcqs.q: Solve: 5x + 8 = 23. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Transfer the constant: 5x = 23 - 8 = 15. Divide by 5: x = 15/5 = 3. Verify: 5(3) + 8 = 15 + 8 = 23, which equals the right-hand side. Solution set = {3}.

mcqs.q: Solve: (3/5)x - 2/3 = 2. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Transfer the constant: (3/5)x = 2 + 2/3 = 8/3. Divide by 3/5, i.e. multiply by 5/3: x = (8/3)(5/3) = 40/9. Verify: (3/5)(40/9) - 2/3 = 8/3 - 2/3 = 2, matching the right-hand side.

mcqs.q: Solve: 6x - 5 = 2x + 9. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Collect x-terms on one side and constants on the other: 6x - 2x = 9 + 5, so 4x = 14 and x = 14/4 = 7/2. Verify: 6(7/2) - 5 = 21 - 5 = 16 and 2(7/2) + 9 = 7 + 9 = 16, both sides equal.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2/(x - 1) = 1/(x - 2). The solution set is
mcqs.why: Cross-multiply (for x not equal to 1, 2): 2(x - 2) = 1(x - 1), so 2x - 4 = x - 1 and x = 3. Verify: 2/(3 - 1) = 1 and 1/(3 - 2) = 1, both sides equal. Solution set = {3}.

mcqs.q: Solve: 1/(7x + 13) = 2/9. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Cross-multiply: 9 = 2(7x + 13) = 14x + 26. So 14x = 9 - 26 = -17 and x = -17/14. Verify: 7(-17/14) + 13 = -17/2 + 13 = 9/2, and 1/(9/2) = 2/9, matching the right-hand side.

mcqs.q: Solve: 10(x - 4) = 4(2x - 1) + 5. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Remove brackets: 10x - 40 = 8x - 4 + 5 = 8x + 1. Collect terms: 10x - 8x = 1 + 40, so 2x = 41 and x = 41/2. Verify: 10(41/2 - 4) = 10(33/2) = 165 and 4(41 - 1) + 5 = 165, both sides equal.

mcqs.q: Awais thought of a number, added 3 to it, then doubled the sum and got 40. The original number was
mcqs.why: Let the number be x. Adding 3 gives x + 3 and doubling gives 2(x + 3) = 40. Divide by 2: x + 3 = 20, so x = 17. Verify: 17 + 3 = 20, doubled is 40, as required.

mcqs.q: The sum of two numbers is -4 and their difference is 6. The numbers are
mcqs.why: Let the larger number be x; the other is x - 6. Sum: x + (x - 6) = -4, so 2x = 2 and x = 1. The other number is 1 - 6 = -5. Verify: 1 + (-5) = -4 and 1 - (-5) = 6, both conditions satisfied. The numbers are 1 and -5.

mcqs.q: The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 81. The integers are
mcqs.why: Let the integers be x, x + 2, x + 4. Sum: x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 81, so 3x + 6 = 81, 3x = 75 and x = 25. The integers are 25, 27, 29. Verify: 25 + 27 + 29 = 81.

mcqs.q: A man is 41 years old and his son is 9 years old. In how many years will the father be three times as old as the son?
mcqs.why: Let the time be t years. Then 41 + t = 3(9 + t) = 27 + 3t. So 41 - 27 = 3t - t, giving 14 = 2t and t = 7. Verify: after 7 years the father is 48 and the son is 16, and 48 = 3 x 16. Answer: in 7 years.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A radical equation contains the unknown under a square-root sign.
  • To solve a radical equation: first isolate the radical term on one side, then square both sides, then solve the resulting equation.
  • Squaring can produce extraneous roots, so every answer must be verified by substituting it back into the original equation.
  • 2 sqrt(a) - 3 = 7 gives sqrt(a) = 5 and a = 25; 8 + 3 sqrt(b) = 20 gives sqrt(b) = 4 and b = 16.
  • When radicals appear on both sides, collect them first: 8 sqrt(r) - 5 = sqrt(r) + 9 gives 7 sqrt(r) = 14, so r = 4.
  • 20 - 3 sqrt(t) = sqrt(t) - 4 gives 24 = 4 sqrt(t), so sqrt(t) = 6 and t = 36.
  • For a radical containing an expression, square the whole radicand: sqrt(2x - 7) = 3 gives 2x - 7 = 9 and x = 8.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Solve the radical equation: 2√a - 3 = 7.

Ans: Method: Isolate the radical term, then square both sides, solve, and verify (squaring can give extraneous roots).
2√a = 7 + 3 = 10
√a = 5
Squaring both sides: a = 25
Verify: 2√25 - 3 = 10 - 3 = 7. ✓
Answer: a = 25

Q: Q2. Solve the radical equation: 8 + 3√b = 20.

Ans: Method: Isolate the radical term, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
3√b = 20 - 8 = 12
√b = 4
Squaring both sides: b = 16
Verify: 8 + 3√16 = 8 + 12 = 20. ✓
Answer: b = 16

Q: Q3. Solve the radical equation: 7 - √(2b) = 3.

Ans: Method: Isolate the radical term, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
√(2b) = 7 - 3 = 4
Squaring both sides: 2b = 16
b = 8
Verify: 7 - √(16) = 7 - 4 = 3. ✓
Answer: b = 8

Q: Q4. Solve the radical equation: 8√r - 5 = √r + 9.

Ans: Method: Collect the radical terms on one side, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
8√r - √r = 9 + 5
7√r = 14
√r = 2
Squaring both sides: r = 4
Verify: 8√4 - 5 = 16 - 5 = 11 and √4 + 9 = 2 + 9 = 11. ✓
Answer: r = 4

Q: Q5. Solve the radical equation: 20 - 3√t = √t - 4.

Ans: Method: Collect the radical terms on one side, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
20 + 4 = √t + 3√t
24 = 4√t
√t = 6
Squaring both sides: t = 36
Verify: 20 - 3√36 = 20 - 18 = 2 and √36 - 4 = 6 - 4 = 2. ✓
Answer: t = 36

Q: Q6. Solve the radical equation: 2√(5x) - 3 = 7.

Ans: Method: Isolate the radical term, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
2√(5x) = 7 + 3 = 10
√(5x) = 5
Squaring both sides: 5x = 25
x = 5
Verify: 2√25 - 3 = 10 - 3 = 7. ✓
Answer: x = 5

Q: Q7. Solve the radical equation: √(2x - 7) + 8 = 11.

Ans: Method: Isolate the radical term, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
√(2x - 7) = 11 - 8 = 3
Squaring both sides: 2x - 7 = 9
2x = 16
x = 8
Verify: √(16 - 7) + 8 = 3 + 8 = 11. ✓
Answer: x = 8

Q: Q8. Solve the radical equation: 22 = 17 + √(40 - 3y).

Ans: Method: Isolate the radical term, then square both sides, solve, and verify.
√(40 - 3y) = 22 - 17 = 5
Squaring both sides: 40 - 3y = 25
3y = 40 - 25 = 15
y = 5
Verify: 17 + √(40 - 15) = 17 + 5 = 22. ✓
Answer: y = 5

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 2 sqrt(a) - 3 = 7
mcqs.why: Isolate the radical: 2 sqrt(a) = 7 + 3 = 10, so sqrt(a) = 5. Square both sides: a = 25. Verify: 2 sqrt(25) - 3 = 10 - 3 = 7, matching the original equation. So a = 25.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 8 + 3 sqrt(b) = 20
mcqs.why: Isolate the radical: 3 sqrt(b) = 20 - 8 = 12, so sqrt(b) = 4. Square both sides: b = 16. Verify: 8 + 3 sqrt(16) = 8 + 3(4) = 20, matching the original equation. So b = 16.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 7 - sqrt(2b) = 3
mcqs.why: Isolate the radical: sqrt(2b) = 7 - 3 = 4. Square both sides: 2b = 16, so b = 8. Verify: 7 - sqrt(16) = 7 - 4 = 3, matching the original equation. So b = 8.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 8 sqrt(r) - 5 = sqrt(r) + 9
mcqs.why: Collect the radical terms: 8 sqrt(r) - sqrt(r) = 9 + 5, so 7 sqrt(r) = 14 and sqrt(r) = 2. Square both sides: r = 4. Verify: 8 sqrt(4) - 5 = 16 - 5 = 11 and sqrt(4) + 9 = 2 + 9 = 11, both sides equal.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 20 - 3 sqrt(t) = sqrt(t) - 4
mcqs.why: Collect the radical terms: 20 + 4 = sqrt(t) + 3 sqrt(t), so 24 = 4 sqrt(t) and sqrt(t) = 6. Square both sides: t = 36. Verify: 20 - 3 sqrt(36) = 20 - 18 = 2 and sqrt(36) - 4 = 6 - 4 = 2, both sides equal.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 2 sqrt(5x) - 3 = 7
mcqs.why: Isolate the radical: 2 sqrt(5x) = 7 + 3 = 10, so sqrt(5x) = 5. Square both sides: 5x = 25, so x = 5. Verify: 2 sqrt(25) - 3 = 10 - 3 = 7, matching the original equation. So x = 5.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: sqrt(2x - 7) + 8 = 11
mcqs.why: Isolate the radical: sqrt(2x - 7) = 11 - 8 = 3. Square both sides: 2x - 7 = 9, so 2x = 16 and x = 8. Verify: sqrt(16 - 7) + 8 = sqrt(9) + 8 = 3 + 8 = 11, matching the original equation.

mcqs.q: Solve the radical equation: 22 = 17 + sqrt(40 - 3y)
mcqs.why: Isolate the radical: sqrt(40 - 3y) = 22 - 17 = 5. Square both sides: 40 - 3y = 25, so 3y = 15 and y = 5. Verify: 17 + sqrt(40 - 15) = 17 + sqrt(25) = 17 + 5 = 22, matching the original equation.

mcqs.q: In solving 2 sqrt(a) - 3 = 7, after isolating the radical term the equation becomes
mcqs.why: Add 3 to both sides: 2 sqrt(a) = 10. Divide both sides by 2: sqrt(a) = 5. This isolated form is then squared to get a = 25, which is verified in the original equation: 2(5) - 3 = 7.

mcqs.q: In solving 22 = 17 + sqrt(40 - 3y), the step just before squaring is
mcqs.why: Subtract 17 from both sides to isolate the radical: sqrt(40 - 3y) = 22 - 17 = 5. Only then are both sides squared, giving 40 - 3y = 25 and finally y = 5.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • If |E| = k with k > 0, then E = k or E = -k; both cases must be solved.
  • If |E| = 0, there is only one case: E = 0. For example |2x - 9| = 0 gives x = 9/2.
  • |x + 3| = 5 gives x + 3 = 5 or x + 3 = -5, so the solution set is {2, -8}.
  • If a coefficient multiplies the absolute value, isolate it first: 4|5x - 2| + 3 = 11 gives |5x - 2| = 2 before splitting into cases.
  • Similarly (2/5)|4x - 3| - 9 = -1 gives |4x - 3| = 20, so x = 23/4 or x = -17/4.
  • Every solution is verified by substituting it back into the original absolute-value equation.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Solve for x: |x + 3| = 5.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k (k ≥ 0), then E = k or E = -k. Solve both cases.
Case 1: x + 3 = 5, so x = 2.
Case 2: x + 3 = -5, so x = -8.
Verify: |2 + 3| = 5 ✓; |-8 + 3| = |-5| = 5 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {2, -8}

Q: Q2. Solve for x: |-5x + 1| = 6.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: -5x + 1 = 6, so -5x = 5 and x = -1.
Case 2: -5x + 1 = -6, so -5x = -7 and x = 7/5.
Verify: |-5(-1) + 1| = |6| = 6 ✓; |-5(7/5) + 1| = |-6| = 6 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {-1, 7/5}

Q: Q3. Solve for x: |(3/4)x - 8| = 1.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: (3/4)x - 8 = 1, so (3/4)x = 9 and x = 12.
Case 2: (3/4)x - 8 = -1, so (3/4)x = 7 and x = 28/3.
Verify: |(3/4)(12) - 8| = |1| = 1 ✓; |(3/4)(28/3) - 8| = |7 - 8| = 1 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {12, 28/3}

Q: Q4. Solve for x: |x - 4| = 3.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: x - 4 = 3, so x = 7.
Case 2: x - 4 = -3, so x = 1.
Verify: |7 - 4| = 3 ✓; |1 - 4| = |-3| = 3 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {7, 1}

Q: Q5. Solve for x: |3x + 4| = 2.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: 3x + 4 = 2, so 3x = -2 and x = -2/3.
Case 2: 3x + 4 = -2, so 3x = -6 and x = -2.
Verify: |3(-2/3) + 4| = |2| = 2 ✓; |3(-2) + 4| = |-2| = 2 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {-2/3, -2}

Q: Q6. Solve for x: |2x - 9| = 0.

Ans: Method: |E| = 0 only when E = 0 (there is only one case).
2x - 9 = 0
2x = 9
x = 9/2
Verify: |2(9/2) - 9| = |0| = 0 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {9/2}

Q: Q7. Solve for x: |(3x - 2)/5| = 7.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: (3x - 2)/5 = 7, so 3x - 2 = 35, 3x = 37 and x = 37/3.
Case 2: (3x - 2)/5 = -7, so 3x - 2 = -35, 3x = -33 and x = -11.
Verify: |(37 - 2)/5| = |7| = 7 ✓; |(-33 - 2)/5| = |-7| = 7 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {37/3, -11}

Q: Q8. Solve for x: 4|5x - 2| + 3 = 11.

Ans: Method: First isolate the absolute-value term, then use |E| = k gives E = k or E = -k.
4|5x - 2| = 11 - 3 = 8
|5x - 2| = 2
Case 1: 5x - 2 = 2, so 5x = 4 and x = 4/5.
Case 2: 5x - 2 = -2, so 5x = 0 and x = 0.
Verify: 4|5(4/5) - 2| + 3 = 4(2) + 3 = 11 ✓; 4|5(0) - 2| + 3 = 4(2) + 3 = 11 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {0, 4/5}

Q: Q9. Solve for x: (2/5)|4x - 3| - 9 = -1.

Ans: Method: First isolate the absolute-value term, then use |E| = k gives E = k or E = -k.
(2/5)|4x - 3| = -1 + 9 = 8
|4x - 3| = 8 × 5/2 = 20
Case 1: 4x - 3 = 20, so 4x = 23 and x = 23/4.
Case 2: 4x - 3 = -20, so 4x = -17 and x = -17/4.
Verify: (2/5)|4(23/4) - 3| - 9 = (2/5)(20) - 9 = 8 - 9 = -1 ✓; (2/5)|4(-17/4) - 3| - 9 = (2/5)(20) - 9 = -1 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {-17/4, 23/4}

mcqs.q: Solve for x: |x + 3| = 5. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Use E = k or E = -k. Case 1: x + 3 = 5 gives x = 2. Case 2: x + 3 = -5 gives x = -8. Verify: |2 + 3| = 5 and |-8 + 3| = |-5| = 5. Solution set = {2, -8}.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: |-5x + 1| = 6. The solution set is
Solve for x: |(3/4)x - 8| = 1. The solution set is
Solve for x: |x - 4| = 3. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Case 1: x - 4 = 3 gives x = 7. Case 2: x - 4 = -3 gives x = 1. Verify: |7 - 4| = 3 and |1 - 4| = |-3| = 3. Solution set = {7, 1}.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: |3x + 4| = 2. The solution set is
Solve for x: |2x - 9| = 0. The solution set is
mcqs.why: An absolute value is 0 only when the expression inside is 0, so there is just one case: 2x - 9 = 0, giving 2x = 9 and x = 9/2. Verify: |2(9/2) - 9| = |0| = 0. Solution set = {9/2}.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: |(3x - 2)/5| = 7. The solution set is
Solve for x: 4|5x - 2| + 3 = 11. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Isolate first: 4|5x - 2| = 8, so |5x - 2| = 2. Case 1: 5x - 2 = 2 gives 5x = 4, so x = 4/5. Case 2: 5x - 2 = -2 gives 5x = 0, so x = 0. Verify: 4|5(4/5) - 2| + 3 = 4(2) + 3 = 11 and 4|0 - 2| + 3 = 11. Solution set = {0, 4/5}.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: (2/5)|4x - 3| - 9 = -1. The solution set is
To solve |x + 3| = 5, the two cases to solve are
mcqs.why: The rule for |E| = k (k > 0) is E = k or E = -k, applied to the whole expression inside the bars. Here E = x + 3 and k = 5, so the cases are x + 3 = 5 (giving x = 2) and x + 3 = -5 (giving x = -8).

lessons.title: Exercise 7.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • On a number line, > and < use an open (hollow) circle because the end point is not included; >= and <= use a solid (filled) circle because the end point is included.
  • An inequality is solved like an equation, except that multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses the inequality sign.
  • Multiplying or dividing by a positive number does not change the inequality sign.
  • In a double inequality the same operation is done to all three parts, e.g. 0 < x/4 - 1 < 1/2 gives 4 < x < 6.
  • When the domain is restricted, only the values in that domain are kept: 7 - 2x >= 1 with x in N gives x <= 3, so the solution set is {1, 2, 3}.
  • A double inequality with both ends included, such as -5 <= x <= 6, is shown as a segment with solid circles at both ends.
  • 3(x - 2) > 15 gives x - 2 > 5 and x > 7, shown with an open circle at 7 and an arrow to the right.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Show the inequality on the number line: x > 0.

Ans: The inequality is already solved: x > 0 means all real numbers greater than 0.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x > 0}.
Number line: put an open (hollow) circle at 0, because 0 is not included, and draw the line with an arrow to the right of 0.
Answer: Open circle at 0, arrow to the right

Q: Q1(ii). Show the inequality on the number line: x < 0.

Ans: The inequality is already solved: x < 0 means all real numbers less than 0.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x < 0}.
Number line: put an open (hollow) circle at 0, because 0 is not included, and draw the line with an arrow to the left of 0.
Answer: Open circle at 0, arrow to the left

Q: Q1(iii). Show the inequality on the number line: (x - 3)/2 ≤ -1.

Ans: Method: Solve like an equation - multiply both sides by the positive number 2 (inequality sign does not change), then add 3 to both sides.
(x - 3)/2 ≤ -1
x - 3 ≤ -2
x ≤ 1
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x ≤ 1}.
Number line: put a solid (filled) circle at 1, because 1 is included (≤), and draw the line with an arrow to the left of 1.
Answer: x ≤ 1; solid circle at 1, arrow to the left

Q: Q1(iv). Show the inequality on the number line: x ≤ -5.

Ans: The inequality is already solved: x ≤ -5 means all real numbers less than or equal to -5.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x ≤ -5}.
Number line: put a solid (filled) circle at -5, because -5 is included (≤), and draw the line with an arrow to the left of -5.
Answer: Solid circle at -5, arrow to the left

Q: Q1(v). Show the inequality on the number line: x ≥ -3.

Ans: The inequality is already solved: x ≥ -3 means all real numbers greater than or equal to -3.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x ≥ -3}.
Number line: put a solid (filled) circle at -3, because -3 is included (≥), and draw the line with an arrow to the right of -3.
Answer: Solid circle at -3, arrow to the right

Q: Q1(vi). Show the inequality on the number line: (3x - 2)/6 > 5/2.

Ans: Method: Multiply both sides by the positive number 6 (inequality sign does not change), then solve.
(3x - 2)/6 > 5/2
3x - 2 > 15
3x > 17
x > 17/3
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x > 17/3}.
Number line: put an open (hollow) circle at 17/3, because 17/3 is not included, and draw the line with an arrow to the right of 17/3.
Answer: x > 17/3; open circle at 17/3, arrow to the right

Q: Q1(vii). Show the inequality on the number line: -5 ≤ x ≤ 6.

Ans: This is a double inequality: x is between -5 and 6, both ends included.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -5 ≤ x ≤ 6}.
Number line: put solid (filled) circles at -5 and at 6, because both are included (≤), and join them with a thick segment; nothing outside the segment is shaded.
Answer: Segment from -5 to 6 with solid circles at both ends

Q: Q1(viii). Show the inequality on the number line: 3 ≥ x ≥ -2.

Ans: Rewrite in increasing order: -2 ≤ x ≤ 3, so x is between -2 and 3, both ends included.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -2 ≤ x ≤ 3}.
Number line: put solid (filled) circles at -2 and at 3, because both are included, and join them with a thick segment.
Answer: Segment from -2 to 3 with solid circles at both ends

Q: Q1(ix). Show the inequality on the number line: 0 < x/4 - 1 < 1/2.

Ans: Method: Solve the double inequality by doing the same operation to all three parts: first add 1 everywhere, then multiply by the positive number 4 (signs do not change).
0 < x/4 - 1 < 1/2
1 < x/4 < 3/2
4 < x < 6
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, 4 < x < 6}.
Number line: put open (hollow) circles at 4 and at 6, because neither is included, and join them with a thick segment.
Answer: 4 < x < 6; open circles at 4 and 6, segment between them

Q: Q1(x). Show the inequality on the number line: 0 < (x + 3)/2 < 3/2.

Ans: Method: Solve the double inequality: multiply all three parts by the positive number 2 (signs do not change), then subtract 3 everywhere.
0 < (x + 3)/2 < 3/2
0 < x + 3 < 3
-3 < x < 0
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -3 < x < 0}.
Number line: put open (hollow) circles at -3 and at 0, because neither is included, and join them with a thick segment.
Answer: -3 < x < 0; open circles at -3 and 0, segment between them

Q: Q2(i). Find the solution set: 7 - 2x ≥ 1, x ∈ N.

Ans: Method: Solve like an equation, but when dividing by a negative number the inequality sign reverses.
7 - 2x ≥ 1
-2x ≥ 1 - 7 = -6
Divide by -2 and reverse the sign: x ≤ 3.
Since x ∈ N = {1, 2, 3, ...}, keep only the natural numbers ≤ 3.
Answer: Solution set = {1, 2, 3}

Q: Q2(ii). Find the solution set: 5x + 4 < 34, x ∈ N.

Ans: Method: Subtract 4 from both sides, then divide by the positive number 5 (sign does not change).
5x + 4 < 34
5x < 30
x < 6
Since x ∈ N, keep the natural numbers less than 6.
Answer: Solution set = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}

Q: Q2(iii). Find the solution set: (8x + 1)/2 < 2x - 1.5, x ∈ R.

Ans: Method: Multiply both sides by the positive number 2 (sign does not change), then collect the x-terms.
(8x + 1)/2 < 2x - 1.5
8x + 1 < 4x - 3
8x - 4x < -3 - 1
4x < -4
x < -1 (dividing by positive 4, sign unchanged)
Number line: open circle at -1, arrow to the left.
Answer: Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x < -1}

Q: Q2(iv). Find the solution set: (4x + 3) ≥ 23, x ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.

Ans: Method: Subtract 3 from both sides, then divide by the positive number 4 (sign does not change).
4x + 3 ≥ 23
4x ≥ 20
x ≥ 5
From the given set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, only 5 and 6 satisfy x ≥ 5.
Answer: Solution set = {5, 6}

Q: Q2(v). Find the solution set: 5x + 1 ≥ 13 - x, x ∈ {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}.

Ans: Method: Add x to both sides, subtract 1, then divide by the positive number 6 (sign does not change).
5x + 1 ≥ 13 - x
6x + 1 ≥ 13
6x ≥ 12
x ≥ 2
From the given set, the values ≥ 2 are 2, 3, 4, 5.
Answer: Solution set = {2, 3, 4, 5}

Q: Q2(vi). Find the solution set: (2x + 6)/2 ≤ (x - 9)/3, x ∈ R.

Ans: Method: Multiply both sides by the L.C.M 6 (positive, so the sign does not change), then solve.
(2x + 6)/2 ≤ (x - 9)/3
3(2x + 6) ≤ 2(x - 9)
6x + 18 ≤ 2x - 18
4x ≤ -36
x ≤ -9 (dividing by positive 4, sign unchanged)
Number line: solid circle at -9, arrow to the left.
Answer: Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x ≤ -9}

Q: Q2(vii). Find the solution set: (x - 1)/3 ≤ (1 - x)/2, x ∈ Z.

Ans: Method: Multiply both sides by the L.C.M 6 (positive, so the sign does not change), then solve.
(x - 1)/3 ≤ (1 - x)/2
2(x - 1) ≤ 3(1 - x)
2x - 2 ≤ 3 - 3x
5x ≤ 5
x ≤ 1 (dividing by positive 5, sign unchanged)
Since x ∈ Z, the solution is all integers up to 1.
Answer: Solution set = {1, 0, -1, -2, -3, ...}

Q: Q3(i). Solve and plot on the number line: x/12 ≤ 1/4.

Ans: Method: Multiply both sides by the positive number 12 (sign does not change).
x/12 ≤ 1/4
x ≤ 12 × 1/4 = 3
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x ≤ 3}.
Number line: put a solid (filled) circle at 3, because 3 is included (≤), and draw the line with an arrow to the left of 3.
Answer: x ≤ 3; solid circle at 3, arrow to the left

Q: Q3(ii). Solve and plot on the number line: x + 7 ≥ 2.

Ans: Method: Subtract 7 from both sides (sign does not change).
x + 7 ≥ 2
x ≥ 2 - 7 = -5
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x ≥ -5}.
Number line: put a solid (filled) circle at -5, because -5 is included (≥), and draw the line with an arrow to the right of -5.
Answer: x ≥ -5; solid circle at -5, arrow to the right

Q: Q3(iii). Solve and plot on the number line: 3(x - 2) > 15.

Ans: Method: Divide both sides by the positive number 3 (sign does not change), then add 2 to both sides.
3(x - 2) > 15
x - 2 > 5
x > 7
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, x > 7}.
Number line: put an open (hollow) circle at 7, because 7 is not included, and draw the line with an arrow to the right of 7.
Answer: x > 7; open circle at 7, arrow to the right
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is x > 7 (the printed x > 6 does not satisfy the step x - 2 > 5).

Q: Q3(iv). Solve and plot on the number line: 1/2 > x/4 > -2.

Ans: Method: Multiply all three parts by the positive number 4 (signs do not change), and rewrite in increasing order.
1/2 > x/4 > -2
2 > x > -8, i.e. -8 < x < 2.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -8 < x < 2}.
Number line: put open (hollow) circles at -8 and at 2, because neither is included, and join them with a thick segment.
Answer: -8 < x < 2; open circles at -8 and 2, segment between them

Q: Q3(v). Solve and plot on the number line: 2.5 ≤ x/2 + 1 ≤ 4.5.

Ans: Method: Subtract 1 from all three parts, then multiply all parts by the positive number 2 (signs do not change).
2.5 ≤ x/2 + 1 ≤ 4.5
1.5 ≤ x/2 ≤ 3.5
3 ≤ x ≤ 7
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, 3 ≤ x ≤ 7}.
Number line: put solid (filled) circles at 3 and at 7, because both are included (≤), and join them with a thick segment.
Answer: 3 ≤ x ≤ 7; solid circles at 3 and 7, segment between them
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is 3 ≤ x ≤ 7 (the printed x ≥ 7 keeps only the right end point and loses the left bound 3).

Q: Q3(vi). Solve and plot on the number line: -2 ≤ x < 2.

Ans: The inequality is already solved: x is between -2 (included) and 2 (not included).
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -2 ≤ x < 2}.
Number line: put a solid (filled) circle at -2, because -2 is included (≤), an open (hollow) circle at 2, because 2 is not included (<), and join them with a thick segment.
Answer: -2 ≤ x < 2; solid circle at -2, open circle at 2, segment between them

mcqs.q: Solve (x - 3)/2 <= -1 and describe its number line
options: x <= 1; solid circle at 1, arrow to the left
x <= -1; open circle at -1, arrow to the left
x >= 1; solid circle at 1, arrow to the right
x <= 5; solid circle at 5, arrow to the left
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by the positive number 2 (sign unchanged): x - 3 <= -2. Add 3: x <= 1. Since the sign is <=, 1 is included, so the number line has a solid circle at 1 with the arrow to the left.

Multiply both sides by the positive number 6 (sign unchanged): 3x - 2 > 15. Add 2: 3x > 17. Divide by 3: x > 17/3. On the number line this is an open circle at 17/3 with an arrow to the right, since 17/3 is not included.

mcqs.q: On a number line, -5 <= x <= 6 is shown as
options: Open circles at -5 and 6, segment between them
Solid circles at -5 and 6, segment between them
A solid circle at -5 and an open circle at 6
mcqs.why: Both signs are <=, so both end points -5 and 6 are included and get solid (filled) circles. Only the values between them satisfy the double inequality, so the two circles are joined by a thick segment and nothing outside is shaded.

mcqs.q: Solve the double inequality 0 < x/4 - 1 < 1/2
mcqs.why: Add 1 to all three parts: 1 < x/4 < 3/2. Multiply all three parts by the positive number 4 (signs unchanged): 4 < x < 6. On the number line: open circles at 4 and 6 joined by a segment, since neither end is included.

mcqs.q: Solve the double inequality 0 < (x + 3)/2 < 3/2
mcqs.why: Multiply all three parts by the positive number 2: 0 < x + 3 < 3. Subtract 3 from all three parts: -3 < x < 0. On the number line: open circles at -3 and 0 joined by a segment, since neither end is included.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of 7 - 2x >= 1 for x in N
mcqs.why: Solve: -2x >= 1 - 7 = -6. Divide by -2 and REVERSE the sign: x <= 3. Since x is in N = {1, 2, 3, ...}, keep only the natural numbers up to 3: solution set = {1, 2, 3}.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of 5x + 4 < 34 for x in N
mcqs.why: Solve: 5x < 34 - 4 = 30, and dividing by the positive number 5 gives x < 6. Since x is in N, keep the natural numbers less than 6: solution set = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Note 6 is excluded because the inequality is strict.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of (8x + 1)/2 < 2x - 1.5 for x in R
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by the positive number 2: 8x + 1 < 4x - 3. Collect terms: 8x - 4x < -3 - 1, so 4x < -4 and x < -1 (dividing by positive 4, sign unchanged). On the number line: open circle at -1, arrow to the left.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of 4x + 3 >= 23 for x in {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}
mcqs.why: Solve: 4x >= 23 - 3 = 20, and dividing by the positive number 4 gives x >= 5. From the given set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, only 5 and 6 satisfy x >= 5. Solution set = {5, 6}.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of 5x + 1 >= 13 - x for x in {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
mcqs.why: Add x to both sides: 6x + 1 >= 13. Subtract 1: 6x >= 12. Divide by the positive number 6: x >= 2. From the given set, the values that are >= 2 are 2, 3, 4, 5. Solution set = {2, 3, 4, 5}.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of (2x + 6)/2 <= (x - 9)/3 for x in R
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by the L.C.M. 6 (positive, sign unchanged): 3(2x + 6) <= 2(x - 9), so 6x + 18 <= 2x - 18. Collect terms: 4x <= -36, so x <= -9. On the number line: solid circle at -9, arrow to the left.

mcqs.q: Find the solution set of (x - 1)/3 <= (1 - x)/2 for x in Z
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by the L.C.M. 6 (positive, sign unchanged): 2(x - 1) <= 3(1 - x), so 2x - 2 <= 3 - 3x and 5x <= 5, giving x <= 1. Since x is in Z, the solution is every integer up to and including 1: {1, 0, -1, -2, -3, ...}.

mcqs.q: Solve x/12 <= 1/4 and describe its number line
options: x <= 3; solid circle at 3, arrow to the left
x <= 3; open circle at 3, arrow to the left
x >= 3; solid circle at 3, arrow to the right
x <= 1/3; solid circle at 1/3, arrow to the left
mcqs.why: Multiply both sides by the positive number 12 (sign unchanged): x <= 12 x 1/4 = 3. Since the sign is <=, 3 is included: solid circle at 3 with the arrow to the left.

mcqs.q: Solve 3(x - 2) > 15
mcqs.why: Divide both sides by the positive number 3 (sign unchanged): x - 2 > 5. Add 2: x > 7. On the number line: open circle at 7, arrow to the right. Note: the book's printed answer x > 6 is incorrect, since x = 6.5 gives 3(4.5) = 13.5, which is not greater than 15; the correct answer is x > 7.

Subtract 1 from all three parts: 1.5 <= x/2 <= 3.5. Multiply all three parts by the positive number 2: 3 <= x <= 7. On the number line: solid circles at 3 and 7 joined by a segment. Note: the book's printed answer keeps only x >= 7, which loses the left bound; the correct solution is 3 <= x <= 7.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 7
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Isolate the absolute value before splitting into cases: (1/2)|x - 6| - 4 = -1 gives |x - 6| = 6, so x = 12 or x = 0.
  • |3x - 1| = 2 gives 3x - 1 = 2 or 3x - 1 = -2, so x = 1 or x = -1/3 (the book's printed key for this question is wrong).
  • sqrt(5x + 3) + 2 = 4 gives sqrt(5x + 3) = 2, then 5x + 3 = 4 and x = 1/5.
  • sqrt(x) = -10 has no solution, because a square root is never negative; its solution set is the empty set.
  • An equation with the unknown under a square-root sign, such as sqrt(2x + 1) - 5 = 4, is a radical equation.
  • |5x/3| = 5 gives 5x/3 = 5 or 5x/3 = -5, so the solution set is {3, -3}; none of the book's printed options for this question is correct.
  • Fractions are cleared by multiplying by the L.C.M.: (x - 8)/3 + (x - 3)/2 = 0 multiplied by 6 gives 5x - 25 = 0, so x = 5.
  • Ages word problem: father 4 times the son's age, and in 20 years twice as old, gives 4x + 20 = 2(x + 20), so the son is 10 and the father is 40.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve for x: (1/2)|x - 6| - 4 = -1.

Options: (a) x = 12 (b) x = 8 and x = 4 (c) x = 12 and x = 0 (d) there is no solution

Correct answer: x = 12 and x = 0

Q: Q1(ii). Solve for x: |3x - 1| = 2.

Options: (a) x = 1 (b) x = 1 and x = -1/3 (c) x = 1 and x = -1 (d) x = 1 and x = 1/3

Correct answer: x = 1 and x = -1/3

Q: Q1(iii). The solution set of √(5x + 3) + 2 = 4 is

Options: (a) {1/5} (b) {-1/5} (c) {2} (d) {1}

Correct answer: {1/5}

Q: Q1(iv). Solve for x: √x = -10.

Options: (a) {-10} (b) {} (c) {100} (d) {10}

Correct answer: {}

Q: Q1(v). √(2x + 1) - 5 = 4 is a

Options: (a) Linear equation (b) Radical equation (c) Cubic equation (d) Quadratic equation

Correct answer: Radical equation

Q: Q1(vi). What is the solution for |x - 7| = 1?

Options: (a) x = 8 (b) x = 6 and x = 8 (c) x = 8 and x = -8 (d) x = 6

Correct answer: x = 6 and x = 8

Q: Q1(vii). The solution set of √(5x + 3) + 2 = 4 is

Options: (a) {1/5} (b) {-1/5} (c) {2} (d) {1}

Correct answer: {1/5}

Q: Q1(viii). The solution set of |5x/3| = 5 is: (a) {3} (b) {5, -5} (c) {4, -4} (d) {-4}.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: 5x/3 = 5, so 5x = 15 and x = 3.
Case 2: 5x/3 = -5, so 5x = -15 and x = -3.
Solution set = {3, -3}. None of the four printed options equals {3, -3}: (a) gives only 3, and (b), (c), (d) are wrong values.
Answer: Solution set = {3, -3}
Note: The book's printed answer is incorrect; the correct answer is {3, -3}, which is not among the printed options (the printed key gives (c) {4, -4}).

Q: Q1(ix). Which one is the solution set of |-x| = 0?

Options: (a) {-1} (b) {1} (c) {} (d) {0}

Correct answer: {0}

Q: Q1(x). Solve for x: (x + 2)/(x - 2) > 0.

Options: (a) (-2, ∞) (b) (-2, 2) (c) (-2, ∞) ∪ (2, ∞) (d) (-∞, -2) ∪ (2, ∞)

Correct answer: (-∞, -2) ∪ (2, ∞)

Q: Note

Ans: In Q1(ii) above, the book's printed key gives option (a). That is incorrect: |3x - 1| = 2 gives 3x - 1 = 2 or 3x - 1 = -2, so x = 1 or x = -1/3, which is option (b), marked in green above.

Q: Q2(i). Solve for x: 5(3x + 1) = 2(x - 4).

Ans: Method: Remove the brackets, transfer x-terms to one side and constants to the other, then divide by the coefficient of x.
15x + 5 = 2x - 8
15x - 2x = -8 - 5
13x = -13
x = -1
Verify: 5(3(-1) + 1) = 5(-2) = -10; 2(-1 - 4) = -10. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {-1}

Q: Q2(ii). Solve for x: (x - 8)/3 + (x - 3)/2 = 0.

Ans: Method: Multiply both sides by the L.C.M 6 to clear the fractions, then solve.
2(x - 8) + 3(x - 3) = 0
2x - 16 + 3x - 9 = 0
5x - 25 = 0
5x = 25
x = 5
Verify: (5 - 8)/3 + (5 - 3)/2 = -1 + 1 = 0. ✓
Answer: Solution set = {5}

Q: Q2(iii). Solve for x: √(2(5x - 1)) = √(2x + 14).

Ans: Method: Square both sides to remove the radicals, solve the linear equation, and verify (also check both radicands are non-negative).
Squaring both sides: 2(5x - 1) = 2x + 14
10x - 2 = 2x + 14
8x = 16
x = 2
Verify: √(2(10 - 1)) = √18 and √(4 + 14) = √18. ✓ Both radicands are positive at x = 2.
Answer: Solution set = {2}

Q: Q2(iv). Solve for x: |2x + 7| = 9.

Ans: Method: If |E| = k, then E = k or E = -k.
Case 1: 2x + 7 = 9, so 2x = 2 and x = 1.
Case 2: 2x + 7 = -9, so 2x = -16 and x = -8.
Verify: |2(1) + 7| = 9 ✓; |2(-8) + 7| = |-9| = 9 ✓.
Answer: Solution set = {1, -8}

Q: Q3(i). Solve and graph on the number line: -1 < (x - 3)/2 < 0.

Ans: Method: Multiply all three parts by the positive number 2 (signs do not change), then add 3 everywhere.
-1 < (x - 3)/2 < 0
-2 < x - 3 < 0
1 < x < 3
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, 1 < x < 3}.
Number line: open (hollow) circles at 1 and at 3, because neither is included, joined by a thick segment.
Answer: 1 < x < 3; open circles at 1 and 3, segment between them

Q: Q3(ii). Solve and graph on the number line: -1 < (x - 4)/5 < 0.

Ans: Method: Multiply all three parts by the positive number 5 (signs do not change), then add 4 everywhere.
-1 < (x - 4)/5 < 0
-5 < x - 4 < 0
-1 < x < 4
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -1 < x < 4}.
Number line: open (hollow) circles at -1 and at 4, because neither is included, joined by a thick segment.
Answer: -1 < x < 4; open circles at -1 and 4, segment between them

Q: Q3(iii). Solve and graph on the number line: 7 < -3x + 1 ≤ 13.

Ans: Method: Subtract 1 from all three parts, then divide by -3. Rule: dividing an inequality by a negative number reverses both inequality signs.
7 < -3x + 1 ≤ 13
6 < -3x ≤ 12
Divide by -3 and reverse the signs: -2 > x ≥ -4, i.e. -4 ≤ x < -2.
Solution set = {x | x ∈ R, -4 ≤ x < -2}.
Number line: solid (filled) circle at -4, because -4 is included (≤), open (hollow) circle at -2, because -2 is not included (<), joined by a thick segment.
Answer: -4 ≤ x < -2; solid circle at -4, open circle at -2, segment between them

Q: Q4. A father is 4 times older than his son. In 20 years he will be twice as old as his son. What ages have they now?

Ans: Method: Let the son's present age be x years; then the father's present age is 4x years. Form an equation for their ages after 20 years.
After 20 years: son = x + 20, father = 4x + 20, and father = 2 × son.
4x + 20 = 2(x + 20)
4x + 20 = 2x + 40
2x = 20
x = 10
Father's age = 4 × 10 = 40 years. Verify: after 20 years, son = 30, father = 60 = 2 × 30. ✓
Answer: Father is 40 years old and son is 10 years old

mcqs.q: Solve for x: (1/2)|x - 6| - 4 = -1
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Isolate: (1/2)|x - 6| = 3, so |x - 6| = 6. Case 1: x - 6 = 6 gives x = 12. Case 2: x - 6 = -6 gives x = 0. Verify: (1/2)|12 - 6| - 4 = 3 - 4 = -1 and (1/2)|0 - 6| - 4 = 3 - 4 = -1. So x = 12 and x = 0.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: |3x - 1| = 2
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused, with the key corrected. Case 1: 3x - 1 = 2 gives 3x = 3, so x = 1. Case 2: 3x - 1 = -2 gives 3x = -1, so x = -1/3. Verify: |3(1) - 1| = 2 and |3(-1/3) - 1| = |-2| = 2. Note: the book's printed key gives only x = 1, which is incomplete and incorrect; both values are needed.

mcqs.q: The solution set of sqrt(5x + 3) + 2 = 4 is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Isolate the radical: sqrt(5x + 3) = 4 - 2 = 2. Square both sides: 5x + 3 = 4, so 5x = 1 and x = 1/5. Verify: sqrt(5(1/5) + 3) + 2 = sqrt(4) + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4. Solution set = {1/5}.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: sqrt(x) = -10. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. A square root of a real number is never negative, so sqrt(x) can never equal -10. Squaring would suggest x = 100, but sqrt(100) = 10, not -10, so that root is extraneous. The solution set is the empty set {}.

mcqs.q: sqrt(2x + 1) - 5 = 4 is a
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. The equation contains the unknown x under a square-root (radical) sign, in sqrt(2x + 1). An equation with the unknown under a radical sign is called a radical equation, solved by isolating the radical and squaring both sides.

mcqs.q: What is the solution of |x - 7| = 1?
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. Case 1: x - 7 = 1 gives x = 8. Case 2: x - 7 = -1 gives x = 6. Verify: |8 - 7| = 1 and |6 - 7| = |-1| = 1. So the solutions are x = 6 and x = 8.

mcqs.q: The solution set of |5x/3| = 5 is
mcqs.why: Case 1: 5x/3 = 5 gives 5x = 15, so x = 3. Case 2: 5x/3 = -5 gives 5x = -15, so x = -3. Solution set = {3, -3}. Note: the book's printed options for this question did not include {3, -3} at all and its printed key {4, -4} is wrong; the mathematically correct set {3, -3} is keyed here.

mcqs.q: Which one is the solution set of |-x| = 0?
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. An absolute value equals 0 only when the inside expression is 0: -x = 0 gives x = 0. Verify: |-0| = 0. So the solution set is {0}.

mcqs.q: Solve for x: (x + 2)/(x - 2) > 0. The solution set is
mcqs.why: Book MCQ reused. The fraction is positive when numerator and denominator have the same sign. Both positive: x + 2 > 0 and x - 2 > 0, i.e. x > 2. Both negative: x + 2 < 0 and x - 2 < 0, i.e. x < -2. So the solution is x < -2 or x > 2, written (-infinity, -2) together with (2, infinity).

mcqs.q: Solve for x: 5(3x + 1) = 2(x - 4). The solution set is
mcqs.why: Remove brackets: 15x + 5 = 2x - 8. Collect terms: 15x - 2x = -8 - 5, so 13x = -13 and x = -1. Verify: 5(3(-1) + 1) = 5(-2) = -10 and 2(-1 - 4) = 2(-5) = -10, both sides equal. Solution set = {-1}.

chapters.title: Unit 8: Linear Graphs and Their Applications

lessons.title: Exercise 8.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In an ordered pair (x, y) the first number is the x-coordinate, called the abscissa, and the second number is the y-coordinate, called the ordinate.
  • Quadrant I has x > 0 and y > 0; Quadrant II has x < 0 and y > 0; Quadrant III has x < 0 and y < 0; Quadrant IV has x > 0 and y < 0.
  • A point with x = 0 lies on the y-axis, a point with y = 0 lies on the x-axis, and the point (0, 0) is the origin itself.
  • To plot a point, move horizontally from the origin by the x-value (right if positive, left if negative), then vertically by the y-value (up if positive, down if negative).
  • The coordinates of a plotted point are read as its horizontal distance from the y-axis and its vertical distance from the x-axis.
  • The distance between two points is found with d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2); equal opposite sides show a quadrilateral is a parallelogram.
  • Joining O(0, 0), A(5, 0), B(5, 5) and C(0, 5) gives a square of side 5 units because all four sides are 5 and each corner is a right angle.
  • Points A(0, 1), B(1, 2), C(2, 1) and D(1, 0) have all sides sqrt(2) and equal diagonals 2, so they form a square, which is also a rectangle.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Determine the x and y coordinates of the point A(-7, 5).

Ans: In an ordered pair (x, y), the first number is the x-coordinate (abscissa) and the second number is the y-coordinate (ordinate).
For A(-7, 5), the first number is -7 and the second number is 5.
Answer: x = -7, y = 5

Q: Q1(ii). Determine the x and y coordinates of the point B(0, 7).

Ans: In an ordered pair (x, y), the first number is the x-coordinate and the second number is the y-coordinate.
For B(0, 7), the first number is 0 and the second number is 7.
Answer: x = 0, y = 7

Q: Q1(iii). Determine the x and y coordinates of the point C(-3, 8).

Ans: In an ordered pair (x, y), the first number is the x-coordinate and the second number is the y-coordinate.
For C(-3, 8), the first number is -3 and the second number is 8.
Answer: x = -3, y = 8

Q: Q1(iv). Determine the x and y coordinates of the point D(-3, -3).

Ans: In an ordered pair (x, y), the first number is the x-coordinate and the second number is the y-coordinate.
For D(-3, -3), the first number is -3 and the second number is -3.
Answer: x = -3, y = -3

Q: Q1(v). Determine the x and y coordinates of the point E(10, 12).

Ans: In an ordered pair (x, y), the first number is the x-coordinate and the second number is the y-coordinate.
For E(10, 12), the first number is 10 and the second number is 12.
Answer: x = 10, y = 12

Q: Q2(i). Mention the quadrant in which the point A(-1, √2) lies.

Ans: Rule: Quadrant I: x > 0, y > 0; Quadrant II: x < 0, y > 0; Quadrant III: x < 0, y < 0; Quadrant IV: x > 0, y < 0.
For A(-1, √2): x = -1 < 0 and y = √2 > 0.
Both signs match Quadrant II.
Answer: Quadrant II

Q: Q2(ii). Mention the quadrant in which the point B(-3, -2) lies.

Ans: Rule: Quadrant III has x < 0 and y < 0.
For B(-3, -2): x = -3 < 0 and y = -2 < 0.
Answer: Quadrant III

Q: Q2(iii). Mention the quadrant in which the point C(5, 5) lies.

Ans: Rule: Quadrant I has x > 0 and y > 0.
For C(5, 5): x = 5 > 0 and y = 5 > 0.
Answer: Quadrant I

Q: Q2(iv). Mention the quadrant in which the point D(3, -5) lies.

Ans: Rule: Quadrant IV has x > 0 and y < 0.
For D(3, -5): x = 3 > 0 and y = -5 < 0.
Answer: Quadrant IV

Q: Q2(v). Mention the quadrant in which the point E(-√5, √7) lies.

Ans: Rule: Quadrant II has x < 0 and y > 0.
For E(-√5, √7): x = -√5 < 0 and y = √7 > 0.
Answer: Quadrant II

Q: Q3(i). Plot the points A, B, C and D on the xy-plane: A(3, 1), B(2, 4), C(-5, 6), D(3, -3).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
To plot A(3, 1): move 3 units right from the origin, then 1 unit up; mark the point A.
To plot B(2, 4): move 2 units right, then 4 units up; mark the point B.
To plot C(-5, 6): move 5 units left, then 6 units up; mark the point C.
To plot D(3, -3): move 3 units right, then 3 units down; mark the point D.
Answer: A(3, 1) in Quadrant I, B(2, 4) in Quadrant I, C(-5, 6) in Quadrant II and D(3, -3) in Quadrant IV are plotted at the stated positions

Q: Q3(ii). Plot the points A, B, C and D on the xy-plane: A(-1, 0), B(0, -1), C(2, -2), D(3, 3).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
To plot A(-1, 0): move 1 unit left from the origin on the x-axis; the point lies on the x-axis.
To plot B(0, -1): move 1 unit down from the origin on the y-axis; the point lies on the y-axis.
To plot C(2, -2): move 2 units right, then 2 units down; mark the point C.
To plot D(3, 3): move 3 units right, then 3 units up; mark the point D.
Answer: A(-1, 0) on the x-axis, B(0, -1) on the y-axis, C(2, -2) in Quadrant IV and D(3, 3) in Quadrant I are plotted at the stated positions

Q: Q3(iii). Plot the points A, B, C and D on the xy-plane: A(4, 4), B(0, 0), C(8, -6), D(-7, 5).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
To plot A(4, 4): move 4 units right, then 4 units up; mark the point A.
B(0, 0) is the origin itself.
To plot C(8, -6): move 8 units right, then 6 units down; mark the point C.
To plot D(-7, 5): move 7 units left, then 5 units up; mark the point D.
Answer: A(4, 4) in Quadrant I, B(0, 0) at the origin, C(8, -6) in Quadrant IV and D(-7, 5) in Quadrant II are plotted at the stated positions

Q: Q4. Plot the points associated with the ordered pairs A(3, 5), B(4, 3), C(5, -5), D(-4, -5), E(-4, 4) and F(0, 5).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
Plot A(3, 5): 3 right, 5 up (Quadrant I).
Plot B(4, 3): 4 right, 3 up (Quadrant I).
Plot C(5, -5): 5 right, 5 down (Quadrant IV).
Plot D(-4, -5): 4 left, 5 down (Quadrant III).
Plot E(-4, 4): 4 left, 4 up (Quadrant II).
Plot F(0, 5): on the y-axis, 5 units above the origin.
Answer: The six points A(3, 5), B(4, 3), C(5, -5), D(-4, -5), E(-4, 4) and F(0, 5) are plotted at the stated positions

Q: Q5. Write the coordinates of the points A, B, C and D in the given graph.

Ans: Read each point from the graph: the x-coordinate is its horizontal distance from the y-axis and the y-coordinate is its vertical distance from the x-axis.
Point A is 3 units right and 2 units up, so A = (3, 2).
Point B is 4 units right and 2 units down, so B = (4, -2).
Point C is on the y-axis, 3 units down, so C = (0, -3).
Point D is 3 units left and 4 units up, so D = (-3, 4).
Answer: A(3, 2), B(4, -2), C(0, -3), D(-3, 4)

Q: Q6. Draw a line segment by joining the points (5, 7) and (-7, 9).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
Plot the point (5, 7): 5 units right, 7 units up.
Plot the point (-7, 9): 7 units left, 9 units up.
Join the two plotted points with a straight ruler.
Answer: The straight line segment joining (5, 7) and (-7, 9) is the required line segment

Q: Q7. Draw a triangle ABC by joining the points A(5, 7), B(8, -3) and C(9, 4).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
Plot A(5, 7): 5 right, 7 up.
Plot B(8, -3): 8 right, 3 down.
Plot C(9, 4): 9 right, 4 up.
Join A to B, B to C and C to A with straight lines.
Answer: Joining A(5, 7), B(8, -3) and C(9, 4) gives triangle ABC with sides AB, BC and CA

Q: Q8. Draw a parallelogram OABC by joining the points O(0, 0), A(3, -4), B(1, -7) and C(-2, -3).

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
Plot O(0, 0), A(3, -4), B(1, -7) and C(-2, -3).
Check with the distance formula d = √(x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²:
|OA| = √(3 - 0)² + (-4 - 0)² = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5
|AB| = √(1 - 3)² + (-7 + 4)² = √(4 + 9) = √13
|BC| = √(-2 - 1)² + (-3 + 7)² = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5
|OC| = √(-2 - 0)² + (-3 - 0)² = √(4 + 9) = √13
Since |OA| = |BC| and |AB| = |OC|, the opposite sides are equal.
Join O to A, A to B, B to C and C to O.
Answer: Joining O(0, 0), A(3, -4), B(1, -7) and C(-2, -3) gives the parallelogram OABC

Q: Q9. Join the points O(0, 0), A(5, 0), B(5, 5) and C(0, 5) to draw a square.

Ans: Scale: 1 small square = 1 unit along x-axis and 1 unit along y-axis.
Plot O(0, 0), A(5, 0) on the x-axis, B(5, 5) and C(0, 5) on the y-axis.
Check the sides: |OA| = 5, |AB| = 5, |BC| = 5, |CO| = 5, so all four sides are equal and each corner is a right angle.
Join O to A, A to B, B to C and C to O.
Answer: Joining O(0, 0), A(5, 0), B(5, 5) and C(0, 5) gives a square of side 5 units

Q: Q10. By drawing the graph, show that the points A(0, 1), B(1, 2), C(2, 1) and D(1, 0) are the vertices of a rectangle.

Ans: Plot A(0, 1), B(1, 2), C(2, 1) and D(1, 0) and join them in order.
Use the distance formula d = √(x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)² to find each side:
|AB| = √(1 - 0)² + (2 - 1)² = √(1 + 1) = √2
|BC| = √(2 - 1)² + (1 - 2)² = √(1 + 1) = √2
|CD| = √(1 - 2)² + (0 - 1)² = √(1 + 1) = √2
|DA| = √(0 - 1)² + (1 - 0)² = √(1 + 1) = √2
Find the diagonals:
|AC| = √(2 - 0)² + (1 - 1)² = √4 = 2
|BD| = √(1 - 1)² + (0 - 2)² = √4 = 2
The diagonals are equal, and |AB|² + |BC|² = 2 + 2 = 4 = |AC|², so the corner angle is a right angle (Pythagoras theorem).
Hence the plotted figure has equal diagonals and right angles.
Answer: A(0, 1), B(1, 2), C(2, 1) and D(1, 0) are the vertices of a rectangle (in fact a square, since all sides are √2)

mcqs.q: What are the x-coordinate and y-coordinate of the point A(-7, 5)?
mcqs.why: In the ordered pair (x, y) the first number is the x-coordinate and the second is the y-coordinate. For A(-7, 5) the first number is -7 and the second number is 5, so x = -7 and y = 5.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point A(-1, sqrt(2)) lie?
mcqs.why: Quadrant II is the region where x < 0 and y > 0. Here x = -1 < 0 and y = sqrt(2) > 0, so both signs match Quadrant II exactly.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point D(3, -5) lie?
mcqs.why: Quadrant IV is the region where x > 0 and y < 0. Here x = 3 > 0 and y = -5 < 0, so the point D(3, -5) lies in Quadrant IV.

mcqs.q: Where does the point B(0, 7) lie?
mcqs.why: A point whose x-coordinate is 0 lies on the y-axis. For B(0, 7), x = 0 and y = 7, so the point is on the y-axis, 7 units above the origin.

mcqs.q: What is the point (0, 0) called?
mcqs.why: The point (0, 0) is where the two axes cross. It has x = 0 and y = 0, lies in no quadrant, and is called the origin.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point D(-3, -3) lie?
mcqs.why: Quadrant III is the region where x < 0 and y < 0. Here x = -3 < 0 and y = -3 < 0, so D(-3, -3) lies in Quadrant III.

mcqs.q: Using the distance formula, what is the length of OA for O(0, 0) and A(3, -4)?
mcqs.why: Distance formula: d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). So |OA| = sqrt((3 - 0)^2 + (-4 - 0)^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5 units.

mcqs.q: The points O(0, 0), A(5, 0), B(5, 5) and C(0, 5) are joined in order. What is the side length of the figure formed?
mcqs.why: Side OA joins (0, 0) to (5, 0), so |OA| = 5. Similarly |AB| = |BC| = |CO| = 5. All four sides are 5 units, so the square formed has side 5 units.

mcqs.q: A point on a graph is 3 units to the right of the y-axis and 2 units above the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
mcqs.why: The x-coordinate is the horizontal distance from the y-axis: 3 units right gives x = 3. The y-coordinate is the vertical distance from the x-axis: 2 units up gives y = 2. Hence the point is (3, 2).

mcqs.q: Where does the point F(0, 5) lie?
mcqs.why: A point with x-coordinate 0 lies on the y-axis. F(0, 5) has x = 0, so it is on the y-axis, 5 units above the origin, and in no quadrant.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point D(-4, -5) lie?
mcqs.why: Quadrant III requires x < 0 and y < 0. For D(-4, -5), x = -4 < 0 and y = -5 < 0, so the point lies in Quadrant III.

mcqs.q: Using the distance formula, what is the length of AB for A(0, 1) and B(1, 2)?
mcqs.why: Distance formula: d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). So |AB| = sqrt((1 - 0)^2 + (2 - 1)^2) = sqrt(1 + 1) = sqrt(2) units.

mcqs.q: For the points A(0, 1), B(1, 2), C(2, 1) and D(1, 0), what is the length of the diagonal AC?
mcqs.why: Distance formula: |AC| = sqrt((2 - 0)^2 + (1 - 1)^2) = sqrt(4 + 0) = sqrt(4) = 2 units. The other diagonal BD is also 2, so the diagonals are equal.

mcqs.q: In which quadrant does the point C(5, 5) lie?
mcqs.why: Quadrant I requires x > 0 and y > 0. For C(5, 5), x = 5 > 0 and y = 5 > 0, so the point lies in Quadrant I.
